companies.name: Unite Us
companies.description: Unite Us is the software and data infrastructure company for coordinating whole-person care across healthcare, government, and community-based organizations. Its platform screens people for social determinants of health, sends closed-loop referrals to community services, and tracks outcomes, with EHR and case-management integrations (Epic, Oracle Health, Meditech, Salesforce) delivered through FHIR APIs, SMART on FHIR apps, and other HL7 protocols aligned with Gravity Project standards. The platform is HIPAA-compliant and HITRUST, SOC 2 Type 2, and NIST CSF certified. API and integration documentation is gated to licensed network partners.

companies.name: Firely
companies.description: Firely is an Amsterdam-based health IT company and one of the original co-developers of the HL7 FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) specification. Co-founded by Ewout Kramer and Martijn Harthoorn (both long-time HL7 FHIR core team members), Firely builds the canonical FHIR toolchain used by payers, providers, health authorities, and digital health vendors worldwide. The Firely platform is anchored by Firely Server (formerly Vonk) — a certified production-grade FHIR server with native support for MongoDB and SQL Server, deployable on Windows, Linux, macOS, Docker, and Kubernetes across on-premise, Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud. Firely Server is G10, ONC, and ISiK certified and supports SMART on FHIR, Bulk Data, CDS Hooks, Subscriptions, Terminology Services, and FHIR Mapping. The product family also includes Simplifier.net (the global FHIR profile registry and package server hosting ~9,000 projects, 40,000+ profiles, and 1,600+ implementation guides), Forge (FHIR profile editor), Firely Terminal (command-line FHIR tool with FQL/FSH/FHIRPath support), the open-source Firely .NET SDK (the de-facto reference C# FHIR library), the firely-cql-sdk for Clinical Quality Language, the Firely Validator API, FHIR Facade, Firely Server Ingest, and Firely Auth. Customers include UCSF, Humana, Roche, NHS, Opala, and the World Health Organization. Firely does not operate a hosted multi-tenant FHIR-as-a-service offering with a public REST endpoint; customers run Firely Server in their own environments. The public developer surface is therefore the Firely software products (Firely Server, .NET SDK, Terminal), the Simplifier.net package and registry APIs, and the open HL7 FHIR REST API contract that every Firely Server instance implements.

companies.name: Kalderos
companies.description: Kalderos is a Chicago-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016, that built what it calls the first Drug Discount Management platform. It helps pharmaceutical manufacturers, covered entities (safety-net healthcare providers), and state Medicaid programs manage compliance across U.S. drug discount programs — most notably 340B — using data, AI, and machine learning to identify noncompliant or duplicate discounts, streamline good-faith-inquiry and dispute resolution, and move rebates transparently between stakeholders. Marquee products include 340B Pay, the Truzo rebate-payment platform, Discount Hub for covered entities, and MDRP and Commercial Discount Monitoring for manufacturers. Kalderos was acquired by Model N in 2024 to expand Model N's revenue-management and 340B capabilities for life sciences. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Kalderos operates a customer-facing application (app.kalderos.com) and previously published developer API documentation that is no longer resolvable post-acquisition.

companies.name: OpenPrescribing
companies.description: OpenPrescribing.net is an open-data service built and operated by the Bennett Institute for Applied Data Science at the University of Oxford. It turns the English Prescribing Dataset published monthly by the NHS Business Services Authority into public dashboards, prescribing-safety measures, and a free RESTful API covering primary-care GP prescribing across England. The API exposes spending, quantity and item counts by BNF code and by NHS organisation (practice, PCN, Sub-ICB Location, ICB, Regional Team), standardised prescribing measures, drug-tariff and price-per-unit data, and organisation reference/boundary lookups, all returned as JSON, CSV or GeoJSON. Home market is the United Kingdom (England prescribing data). It is an independent academic analytics platform layered on NHS open data, not an NHS FHIR clinical system; there is no OAuth, no SMART-on-FHIR, and currently no registration or API key is required.

companies.name: Dentsply Sirona
companies.description: Dentsply Sirona is the world's largest manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, providing comprehensive solutions for dentists, dental laboratories, and dental specialists worldwide. The company exposes developer integrations through DS Core, an open cloud platform, and through the Dentsply Sirona Imaging modality API for intraoral imaging hardware.

companies.name: Insight Health
companies.description: Insight Health builds AI clinical agents that handle the patient-facing workflows clinical staff spend the most time on: phone answering, fax processing, ambient note-taking, intake, follow-up, referral management, and triage. Built by practicing physicians, the platform is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and integrates with the major outpatient EHRs via FHIR R4 and HL7v2. Its voice agent Lumi handled the first known autonomous clinical AI conversation with a patient in October 2023, and the company has since handled more than 4 million patient conversations across 60+ medical specialties. Products include Aura AI Scribe, the Aura Anywhere embedded scribe SDK for EHR vendors, AI FrontDesk, AI Fax Agent, Pre-Visit Intake, Follow-up, Referral Management, and Phone Triage agents.

companies.name: Modern Health
companies.description: Modern Health is a global mental health benefits platform that employers offer to their workforce, positioning itself as "the global standard in mental health" with evidence-based, equitable care delivered worldwide. Its Adaptive Care Model spans self-guided digital tools, 1:1 coaching, therapy and counseling, group support Circles, and crisis care, matched to members through a Stepped Care methodology. The platform serves employers, benefits consultants, health plans, and providers, delivering care in 80+ languages across a proprietary provider network spanning 200+ countries and territories. Modern Health does not publish a public developer API; its surfaces are member and admin web/mobile applications, a status page, and a security/trust program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and enriched with the company's real operational, security, and legal surface.

companies.name: Radical Health
companies.description: Radical Health is a Khosla Ventures-backed healthcare AI company that produces personalized, expert-reviewed cancer treatment reports for patients in the United States. Its platform ingests a patient's medical records and synthesizes oncology research, clinical trials, and prior patient outcomes into a tailored report within days, drawing on 5.3 million research papers, 11.8 million patient journeys, 20,000 treatment options, and 48,800+ active US clinical trials. The service pairs an always-on AI nurse navigator ("Alice") with human oncology oversight from institutions including UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Kaiser Permanente, and connects to 70,000+ US healthcare institutions (Epic, Kaiser, Ascension, HCA, Medicare) for records access. Reports are informational and educational only, not medical advice. Radical Health is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified and operates as a consumer subscription product ($110/month with a 7-day free trial); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Counsel Health
companies.description: Counsel Health is a telemedicine company multiplying the world's healthcare capacity by pairing an AI medical assistant with board-certified physicians delivered through chat. Individuals get free AI medical guidance and can connect with a licensed doctor for a flat $29 per consultation, seven days a week, for urgent care, primary care support, medication refills, lab testing, and health-record management. Counsel also ships an embedded product — a WebView / iFrame surface plus a server-side Counsel API — that partners integrate into their own applications, documented at docs.counselhealth.com with example apps published on GitHub. Backed by GV (Google Ventures).

companies.name: OSCAR EMR
companies.description: OSCAR EMR is an open-source electronic medical record (EMR) system created by Dr. David Chan and McMaster University's Department of Family Medicine, and one of Canada's most widely deployed primary-care EMRs. The core software is distributed under the GPL v2+ license (mirrored on GitHub as scoophealth/oscar and on Bitbucket), while the commercially supported OSCAR Pro distribution is delivered by the WELL EMR Group (a WELL Health company) to more than 2,000 clinics and 10,000 providers across Canada. OSCAR exposes a documented REST web-services API under the /ws/services path (scheduling, demographics, billing, prescriptions, documents, labs, ticklers, eForms and providers), secured with 3-legged OAuth 1.0a via /ws/oauth. Clinical data flows historically use HL7 v2 messaging, and OSCAR ships an internal HL7 FHIR integration used for Ontario public-health and immunization reporting (BORN, DHIR). Third-party integrations for OSCAR Pro are partner-gated through the apps.health marketplace. As self-hosted software there is no single public API host or hosted FHIR CapabilityStatement; the API surface is documented on the OSCAR EMR developer wiki and realized per clinic deployment.

companies.name: Anthem
companies.description: Anthem, Inc. (now operating as Elevance Health) is one of the largest health benefits companies in the United States, serving members through affiliated Blue Cross and Blue Shield health plans across multiple states including California, New York, Virginia, Georgia, and others. Anthem provides health insurance, pharmacy benefits, and behavioral health services to over 40 million members. Under CMS interoperability rules (CMS-9115-F), Anthem offers FHIR- based Patient Access and Provider Directory APIs.

companies.name: Defense Health Agency
companies.description: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is a joint, integrated combat support agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to combatant commands. DHA operates the Military Health System (MHS), MHS Genesis electronic health record, the Military Health System Data Repository (MDR), and the Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions (EIDS) program. Data exchange inside MHS Genesis uses SMART on FHIR APIs, but DHA does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer API.

companies.name: Medigate
companies.description: Medigate was a healthcare IoT / connected-medical-device cybersecurity company (headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, backed by Partech and others) that built the first security platform dedicated to healthcare IoT — device discovery, risk assessment, and clinically-aware network segmentation for hospitals. Claroty completed its acquisition of Medigate on 2022-01-10 and folded the product into "Claroty xDome for Healthcare"; the standalone brand is retired and medigate.io now redirects to claroty.com. A residual customer-facing REST API remains live at api.medigate.io (with a password-gated interactive reference at api.medigate.io/docs) that integrations use to pull device inventory, device groups, and device risk scores.

companies.name: Stryker
companies.description: Stryker Corporation is a Fortune 500 medical technologies company offering products in orthopedics, medical and surgical equipment, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker provides Connected OR integration platforms and Smart Equipment Management (SEM) systems for healthcare facilities. The company does not currently offer a publicly documented developer API. Stryker's digital health products include the Mako robotic arm for orthopedic surgery, iSuite integrated OR technology, and asset tracking systems. Integration with hospital EHR and OR management systems is done through vendor partnerships rather than public APIs.

companies.name: Vivoo
companies.description: Vivoo is a wellness technology company offering science-backed, at-home urine test strips paired with a mobile app that turns results into personalized nutrition and lifestyle recommendations. Its lineup includes the 8-parameter Vivoo Wellness Test, an at-home UTI test, fertility/ovulation and vaginal pH tests, and a connected Smart Toilet. The direct-to-consumer store runs on Shopify and exposes a native agent-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and a hosted UCP shopping MCP server for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout. Backed by 500 Global and Techstars.

companies.name: CareFusion (BD)
companies.description: CareFusion is a medical technology brand, acquired by BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) in 2015, best known for the Alaris infusion system and the Pyxis automated dispensing product line. CareFusion does not expose a public developer API; instead, its devices and dispensing systems interoperate with hospital EMRs and pharmacy systems over HL7 v2 messaging, smart-pump interoperability middleware, and vendor-managed integration services. The Alaris Infusion Interoperability program wirelessly transmits orders from EMRs (such as Epic and Cerner) into Alaris large-volume and syringe modules and returns infusion status back to the EMR in near real time, using the Alaris Guardrails drug library as a safety layer.

companies.name: Mio
companies.description: Mio is a collaboration interoperability platform that connects the leading enterprise messaging tools so teams on different platforms can work together without switching apps. Positioned as Google's official interoperability partner, Mio provides API-based middleware that relays messages, files, and directory information between Google Chat, Microsoft Teams, Slack, and Zoom Team Chat. Its products include Chat Sync (cross-platform messaging), External Chat Sync (partner/federated collaboration), Directory Sync (bidirectional user directory synchronization), and File Sync (shared Google Drive and SharePoint links). Mio runs as native middleware built directly with the platform vendors, never persistently stores user messages or files, encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2+ and at rest with AES-256, and holds SOC 2 Type II certification with GDPR and CCPA controls. Mio is sold as an enterprise offering rather than a self-serve public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and support surface.

companies.name: TrueCoach
companies.description: TrueCoach is a personal-training and remote-coaching platform for strength coaches, personal trainers, and physical therapists to deliver workouts online and train clients remotely. Started as Fitbot out of Techstars Boulder and now an Xplor Technologies brand, it offers a web app plus iOS and Android client apps with program and workout builders, a video exercise library, nutrition tracking, wearables data, Stripe-powered payments, a MyFitnessPal integration, and a Zapier connector — but publishes no public developer API.

companies.name: Snap-on
companies.description: Snap-on Incorporated is a global manufacturer and marketer of tools, equipment, diagnostics, repair information, and systems solutions for professional users in vehicle repair, industrial, and other industries. The company provides diagnostic tools, electronic parts catalogs (EPC), repair information systems (ShopKey Pro, SureTrack), and shop management software. Snap-on integrates with dealer management systems (DMS) through its EPC integration program and strategic technology partnerships.

companies.name: WebPT
companies.description: WebPT is a rehabilitation-therapy software company providing a cloud practice-management platform for physical, occupational, and speech therapy and behavioral-health clinics. Its integrated suite spans clinical documentation and EMR, billing and revenue-cycle management, front-office scheduling and digital patient intake, benefits verification, home exercise programs, patient engagement and outcomes tracking, marketing, and practice analytics. WebPT connects to 60+ EHR and healthcare systems (Epic, athenahealth, Veradigm, McKesson, Meditech, Oracle Cloud, ModMed and others) through an integrations program built on HL7 interfaces (ADT, BAR, DFT, MDM/ORU). WebPT does not publish a public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition; integration is arranged through its partner and integrations program. WebPT is a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

companies.name: Hammerhead
companies.description: Hammerhead is a cycling technology company (now part of SRAM) best known for the Karoo GPS cycling computer, a premium Android-based device for recording and displaying ride data, routes, structured workouts, and Flight Attendant performance. Its ecosystem includes the web Dashboard (dashboard.hammerhead.io) and a Companion mobile app that bridge ride data between rider, device, and third parties. Hammerhead runs one of the more open developer platforms in the category: a public API that lets connected third parties sync routes and workouts, and the karoo-ext Android/Kotlin Extensions SDK (io.hammerhead:karoo-ext, Apache-2.0) that lets developers build on-device extensions for Karoo and Karoo 2.

companies.name: kaiahealth
companies.description: Kaia Health is a digital therapeutics company founded in 2016 (New York and Munich) that delivers evidence-based, digital-first care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain and respiratory conditions. Its smartphone apps use AI and computer vision (motion tracking) plus in-house physical-therapy doctors to guide members through clinically validated exercise and behavioral programs without appointments or wearable devices. Products include Kaia MSK (joint and muscle care) and Kaia Breathe (respiratory / COPD). The company sells to employers and health plans, claims 2,500+ enterprise clients and 3x ROI, and is HIPAA, GDPR, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 13485, and CE-certified. Kaia Health was acquired by Sword Health in January 2026. It is backed by Balderton Capital. Kaia Health publishes no public API; this profile captures its identity, security, and compliance posture.

companies.name: La Fraise Pro
companies.description: La Fraise (LA FRAISE PRO SAS) is a French SaaS platform that digitizes the administrative patient journey for dental practices and dental centers: interactive treatment quotes (devis), patient-education video, informed consent, mutual-insurer coverage requests, and compliant electronic signature, all handled remotely. The product integrates natively with the French dental practice-management market — LOGOSw, Julie, Veasy, CS Trophy, Visiodent, Ardion, WeClever, Desmos, Galaxie and Effigie — with real-time bidirectional sync for LOGOSw, Veasy and Desmos. More than 3,500 dentists are equipped. Patient data is hosted on HDS-certified AWS infrastructure in the European Union, in line with article L.1111-8 of the French Code de la sante publique, and electronic signature follows Agence du Numerique en Sante (ANS) norms. La Fraise publishes no public developer API; practice-management integrations are provisioned by its own technical team.

companies.name: Magical
companies.description: Magical is an AI-agent platform that automates repetitive administrative and operational workflows without requiring API integrations, instead driving the same web applications and databases a human worker would use. Originally known for its cross-application autofill and text-automation product, Magical has focused on healthcare operations, deploying specialized AI agents for patient access, revenue cycle management, prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, records requests, revenue integrity, and payment posting across EHR and payer systems such as Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, Availity, and major insurers. Agents can be deployed individually or combined into autonomous suites, with the company reporting high task accuracy and multi-week deployment timelines. Magical is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and SV Angel. Notably, Magical operates through user-interface automation ("no APIs or integrations are required") rather than by exposing a public developer API.

companies.name: Apero
companies.description: Apero Health is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed healthcare technology company that provides an integrated practice-management and revenue-cycle-management (RCM) platform for medical practices. Its cloud software unifies scheduling, clinical visit notes, insurance eligibility verification and claims billing, patient billing and payments, e-prescriptions, and financial reporting, and claims to reduce billing time by up to 80% while helping practices scale operations. Apero exposes a fully-featured REST API, webhooks, and CSV import that connect healthcare and finance workflows, and integrates with payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and platforms including Stripe, QuickBooks Online, Google, and Snowflake.

companies.name: Beacon Health
companies.description: Beacon Health (YC W26) is a San Francisco company building "AI employees" for primary care — autonomous agents that operate directly inside electronic health record systems the same way a human staff member does. Rather than integrating through an EHR vendor API, Beacon records a practice's existing workflow in the EHR (navigation, clicks, data entry) and converts that recording into a reusable, deployable agent that runs at scale across the whole patient panel. The agents automate value-based-care back-office work: preventative and quality gap closure, pre-charting, prior authorizations, referrals, transition-of-care management, and HCC risk-adjustment coding. Beacon advertises coverage of AthenaHealth, Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, MEDITECH, NextGen, Veradigm Allscripts and MEDENT, plus payer portals and other web applications. Founded in 2025 by Mark Pothen (CEO) and Obinna Akahara (CTO), the company operates as a HIPAA Business Associate under a BAA with each covered entity. As of this profile Beacon Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition — the product is delivered as a managed agent workforce, not as a self-serve API.

companies.name: Ecton
companies.description: Ecton, Inc. is an AI-powered patient payments platform focused on reducing the financial stress and financial toxicity that surround healthcare costs. Its flagship product, Toni, is an AI financial counselor that gives patients personalized guidance on medical bills, insurance, and payment options, paired with a Health Savings and Spending Wallet for managing and paying healthcare expenses. Ecton helps healthcare providers strengthen patient relationships, improve treatment adherence, and increase revenue collection. The company is HIPAA-aligned and backed by General Catalyst. Ecton does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and public security posture.

companies.name: Fortuna Health
companies.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.

companies.name: HumanFirst
companies.description: HumanFirst is a digital health measurement company whose Atlas platform helps clinical research and life-sciences teams evaluate, select, and operationalize sensor-based digital health technologies — wearables, connected devices, and digital biomarkers — for clinical trials and real-world evidence. Atlas curates a knowledge network of digital measures, connected devices, and the published evidence behind them so sponsors and CROs can choose fit-for-purpose measures. HumanFirst is now part of ICON plc and integrated into ICON's Digital Health Technologies (DHT) capabilities. The Atlas platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at app.gohumanfirst.com; the company does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: IDOVEN
companies.description: Idoven builds artificial-intelligence solutions for cardiovascular care. Its flagship platform, Willem, is a CE-marked Class IIa medical device that analyzes electrocardiograms (ECGs) to detect, diagnose, and monitor cardiac disease, identifying 22 cardiac patterns and 4 intervals across ambulatory devices, diagnostic ECGs, and insertable cardiac monitors. Idoven serves MedTech companies, Life Sciences (cardiotoxicity monitoring and disease-risk scoring for pharma trials), and preventative remote-screening programs. The Willem API supports bi-directional data exchange in EDF, HL7, DICOM, JSON, XML, and PDF. The company is headquartered in Spain, holds an extensive ISO and IEC certification program, and is backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Sector: healthcare / cardiology AI.

companies.name: MedicalDirector
companies.description: MedicalDirector is an Australian clinical and practice-management software provider, owned by Telstra Health, that has served general practices, specialists, and day hospitals across Australia for more than 25 years. Its product family includes Helix (a cloud-based combined clinical and practice-management system), Clinical and Pracsoft (on-premise clinical and practice-management software), Bluechip (specialist practice management), and Day Surgery. Alongside Best Practice, MedicalDirector is one half of the dominant Australian GP-software duopoly. Its programmatic surface is delivered through Telstra Health Smart API+, a FHIR-native integration gateway that lets approved technology partners exchange data with MedicalDirector Helix (and, on a case-by-case basis, MedicalDirector Clinical) without bespoke, platform-specific integrations. Smart API+ is a gated, partner-onboarded API: it is publicly announced and described but has no self-serve public developer portal, and no FHIR CapabilityStatement or OpenAPI is published anonymously. Access is granted through a partner agreement, and the underlying FHIR version and SMART-on-FHIR auth specifics are not disclosed on public pages.

companies.name: Infinitus
companies.description: Infinitus Systems is a safety-first healthcare voice AI platform that automates outbound and inbound phone calls to patients, payors, and providers for clinical and administrative tasks including benefit verification, prior authorization, prescription follow-up, and patient engagement. Its products include AI Agents (autonomous call handling), AI Copilots (human-assisted tools), Studio (a no-code agent builder), and Lens (conversation analysis and real-time clinical risk detection), backed by a healthcare knowledge graph. Benefit verification can be invoked as individual or bulk requests through an API, and the platform offers a Salesforce integration, though Infinitus does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI. The company is backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins.

companies.name: Gradient Health
companies.description: Gradient Health is a multimodal medical data company that accelerates medical AI development by giving AI developers secure, self-service access to diverse, de-identified medical imaging data. Its Atlas platform lets teams search a catalog of 20M+ de-identified imaging studies across hundreds of DICOM tags with longitudinal, patient-level search, construct representative cohorts, and export full DICOM datasets. Gradient Health sources, de-identifies, curates, and delivers data from a network of healthcare data partners, and is HIPAA compliant and AICPA SOC 2 certified. First-party open-source tooling supports cloud-optimized DICOM storage, parsing, and TensorFlow decode operations.

companies.name: OpenFin
companies.description: OpenFin — now branded HERE — is the operating-system layer for enterprise financial desktops. Its container/runtime lets web applications run as secure, interoperable desktop apps, adding Workspace surfaces (Home, Dock, Store, Notifications Center, Browser) and FDC3-based application interop. The developer surface is a JavaScript `fin` runtime/container API (with Java and .NET adapters and a rich set of @openfin npm packages), not a REST/HTTP API. OpenFin is deployed across banks and financial institutions and is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. This profile was enriched from OpenFin/HERE's public developer surface.

companies.name: Axxess

companies.name: Standardization
companies.description: Standardization is the process of implementing and developing technical standards based on the consensus of different parties, including firms, users, interest groups, standards organizations, and governments. The goal is to establish uniform engineering or technical criteria, methods, processes, and practices. Key standards bodies include ISO (International Organization for Standardization), IEEE, IETF, W3C, OASIS, and national bodies such as ANSI, BSI, and DIN. In the API space, standardization covers OpenAPI Specification (OAS), AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and emerging protocols including MCP. Proper standardization reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness, interoperability, and long-term maintainability.

companies.name: HealthVerity

Unlike EHR and FHIR-network players, it exposes no public developer portal, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no downloadable OpenAPI; the only vendor-named programmatic surface is the gated, enterprise HealthVerity Identity API for real-time de-identification, described conceptually on the Identity Manager product page but without public reference documentation, base URL, or self-serve onboarding.

companies.name: Tendo

Surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: WELL Health Technologies
companies.description: WELL Health Technologies Corp (TSX: WELL, OTCQX: WHTCF) is a Vancouver, Canada-headquartered healthcare technology company that is Canada's largest outpatient medical clinic owner-operator and a leading multi-disciplinary digital health service provider. It runs two synergistic channels: an omni-channel patient services business operating 115+ multidisciplinary clinics across Canada plus US telehealth and anesthesia operations, and a virtual-services / practitioner-enablement platform serving 44,000+ providers through the OSCAR Pro EMR, billing and revenue-cycle tools, eReferral, digital booking, and ePharma. companies.name: AcuityMD

Used by 500+ medical device companies, the platform spans Market Intelligence, Care Journeys, Targeting, Pipeline, Contracts, Territories and Forecasting. AcuityMD is a closed enterprise SaaS product: it exposes no public developer API, but integrates via a Salesforce AppExchange app, a Snowflake Marketplace listing, and an enterprise Data Connector that delivers market intelligence into customer data warehouses. Backed by ICONIQ Capital and Redpoint Ventures.

companies.name: Artera
companies.description: Artera is a healthcare technology company providing an AI-powered patient communication and engagement platform used by hospitals, health systems, and medical practices to unify how they reach and care for patients. The platform orchestrates SMS, voice, email, and chat across the patient journey — appointment scheduling and reminders, patient intake, payments, referral management, care-gap closure, prescription refills, multilingual engagement, and after-hours call routing and triage — increasingly through agentic AI. Artera connects to the EHR and patient-facing vendors via API, FHIR, and HL7v2 integrations with major systems including Epic, Oracle Health, MEDITECH, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Veradigm, NextGen, Greenway, ModMed, AdvancedMD, and Netsmart. The company maintains a strong security and compliance posture (SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, FedRAMP, HIPAA). It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: MeetAsh
companies.description: Ash (MeetAsh / Ash Wellness) is a New York-based health technology company, founded in 2019, that powers white-label at-home health testing programs for health plans, digital health companies, and public health organizations. Through a single, developer-friendly REST API integration, partners can trigger test kits, manage shipping logistics, and securely transmit results back into an EHR or patient portal across a national network of CLIA- and CAP-certified laboratories. Ash offers 120+ at-home diagnostic panels (hormone, cancer, allergy, STI, chronic condition, and infectious-disease testing with self-collected blood, stool, urine, saliva, and swab samples), care-gap-closure programs for HEDIS measures, kitting and fulfillment, physician-of-record services, and real-time reporting dashboards. The platform is fully HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with enterprise-grade encryption protecting PHI. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network; the developer documentation is partner-gated (password protected).

companies.name: Dentrix
companies.description: Dentrix is a dental practice management platform from Henry Schein One, used by dental offices to manage patients, scheduling, clinical charting, treatment planning, insurance, and billing. Dentrix exposes third-party integration APIs through two distinct channels. The original Dentrix Developer Program (DDP, launched 2012) targets the on-premise Dentrix desktop application: integrations run locally against the office's Dentrix database over password-protected ODBC connections, stored procedures, table views, and DLL functions (authenticated via a RegisterUser call) - it is NOT a public REST/cloud API, and cloud integrations require a locally installed desktop agent. The newer Dentrix Ascend API Exchange (launched July 2023) is a cloud, REST/JSON API over HTTPS secured with OAuth 2.0 on the SOC 2 Type II Dentrix Ascend platform, exposing patient, scheduling, claims, and inventory data. Both channels are partner-gated: access requires an application, a signed agreement, and paid developer fees. There is no public self-serve API key or published OpenAPI, so the APIs below are modeled from Henry Schein One's public developer materials rather than an official machine-readable specification.

companies.name: Omada Health
companies.description: Omada Health is a virtual-first healthcare company founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco that delivers integrated, evidence-based care programs for chronic disease management. Omada combines one-on-one health coaching, connected smart devices (cellular scales, blood pressure monitors, glucose meters), interactive lessons, and peer communities to support people managing prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, and musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, along with GLP-1 medication support and weight health. The company sells to employers, health plans, benefit consultants, and health systems rather than to individual consumers directly, and operates as a HIPAA covered entity and business associate. Omada Health is publicly traded and is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It has no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity, security/compliance posture, and operational transparency pages.

companies.name: Tuva Health
companies.description: Tuva Health, Inc. is a United States healthcare data company behind The Tuva Project, an open-source, warehouse-native data-transformation platform that harmonizes, validates, normalizes, and enriches raw healthcare data - medical and pharmacy claims, EHR clinical data, ADT feeds, and HL7 FHIR sources - into an analytics-ready Core Data Model and a library of Data Marts (AHRQ measures, readmissions, quality measures, chronic conditions, CCSR, pharmacy). It is delivered primarily as a dbt package plus Python utilities (FHIR Inferno) and a family of source connectors that run inside the customer's own cloud data warehouse - Snowflake, Databricks, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, or Microsoft Fabric - rather than as a hosted service. Tuva is not an HTTP or FHIR API vendor: FHIR R4 is a supported input format that Tuva flattens and maps into its Input Layer, not a live FHIR server it operates. The company pairs the open-source project with a commercial Core Platform. Home market is the United States.

companies.name: 9am Health
companies.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

companies.name: Theator
companies.description: Theator is a surgical intelligence platform that turns minimally invasive surgical video into structured, actionable intelligence. The company processes operative video footage into procedural insights, outcomes data, and surgery-to-text documentation for three audiences: surgeons seeking objective performance feedback, hospital and health-system executives tracking outcomes and efficiency, and revenue-cycle teams improving documentation and coding. Theator is a healthcare technology company backed by Insight Partners and partners with AWS and Oracle Health. It maintains a formal security and compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) published via its trust center. No public first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been identified; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

companies.name: Chefaa
companies.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

companies.name: Ellipsis Health
companies.description: Ellipsis Health is a healthcare AI company that has established the human voice as a vital sign for mental health, using clinically validated vocal-biomarker technology, natural language processing, and acoustic models to identify, measure, and monitor the severity of depression and anxiety from short samples of natural speech. Its flagship product, Sage, is an emotionally intelligent, agentic AI care manager that conducts 24/7 patient-engagement calls for health plans, health systems, specialty care, and pharma, handling program enrollment, benefits verification, clinical assessments and surveys, and care coordination. Sage is powered by Ellipsis' patented Empathy Engine, trained on millions of live clinical patient calls, and runs on HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant infrastructure. Ellipsis Health integrates with health plans and systems such as Cigna, and exposes a private partner API (used by partners like Augmedix) rather than a public developer platform. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and CVS Health Ventures.

companies.name: Force Therapeutics
companies.description: Force Therapeutics is a healthcare technology company providing a digital patient-engagement and remote-monitoring platform for surgical and musculoskeletal care. The platform delivers personalized patient education, automated collection of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs), preoperative optimization, postoperative recovery management, direct patient messaging, and actionable clinical insights for hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and private practices. Force integrates with major EHR systems (Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, NextGen) through the Redox Connection Network and FHIR/HL7-based workflows rather than a public developer API. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant, hosted on Amazon Web Services, and backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Nolla Health
companies.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

companies.name: Ritten
companies.description: Ritten is a cloud-based electronic medical record (EMR) and practice-management platform built specifically for behavioral health and substance-use treatment organizations — detox, residential, PHP/IOP, and outpatient providers. Its browser-based product covers clinical documentation (group and individual notes, AI-assisted charting), scheduling, revenue-cycle management (claims, billing, authorizations), a HIPAA-compliant patient portal, treatment planning, compliance tooling (audit trails, signature routing), and outcomes reporting. Ritten is built for HIPAA-regulated and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality requirements with role-based access controls and audit logs, and supports operational integrations for e-prescribing, labs, eligibility/billing clearinghouses, and telehealth. Ritten does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by 8VC and Threshold Ventures; based in Philadelphia, PA.

companies.name: TELUS Health
companies.description: TELUS Health is the digital-health division of TELUS, one of Canada's largest telecommunications and technology companies, and the country's leading health-IT provider. It operates the PS Suite, Med Access, and cloud-native Collaborative Health Record (CHR) electronic medical records used across Canadian primary care, along with pharmacy management, virtual care, and employer/benefits health services. Its documented public integration surface is the CHR Enterprise API, a GraphQL endpoint secured with RS512-signed JWT bearer tokens that exposes clinic data (patients, appointments, encounters, clinical documents and more) for partner-built add-ons, complemented by the TELUS Patient Chart FHIR R4 implementation guide, a package of 89 published StructureDefinition profiles under the http://telus.com/fhir/patientChart canonical for standards-based patient-record exchange out of TELUS EMRs, and the Omara Health Exchange FHIR interoperability platform. Home market is Canada, where healthcare is province-fragmented and FHIR interoperability is stewarded federally by Canada Health Infoway. Both API surfaces are documented but gated behind a partner or CHR-domain agreement.

companies.name: nference
companies.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

companies.name: Virta Health
companies.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

companies.name: Carepatron
companies.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.

companies.name: Commure
companies.description: Commure is a San Francisco-based AI-native healthcare technology company that operates an integrated clinical and operational platform for United States health systems following its 2023 combination with Athelas. Its products span Ambient AI clinical documentation (Scribe/Dictation), end-to-end Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Call Center Agents, referral Orchestrator, patient Engage coordination, Commure Pro clinical intelligence, Strongline staff-safety alerting, and Athelas Home point-of-care diagnostics, integrating with 60+ EHRs across 130+ health systems processing over $25B in annual claims. Commure launched a FHIR-native open developer platform in 2020, but that public developer portal (developer.commure.com) is no longer live; today the API surface is a gated, partner-only offering governed by a Developer User Agreement (Sandbox Environment + Developer Services), with no self-serve public API documentation, FHIR CapabilityStatement, or downloadable OpenAPI currently published. Home market is the United States.

companies.name: Margo
companies.description: Margo is a Linux Foundation open standard initiative for interoperability at the edge of industrial automation ecosystems. Founded by ABB, Capgemini, Microsoft, Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, it defines mechanisms for interoperability between edge applications, devices, and orchestration software.

companies.name: Parachute Health
companies.description: Parachute Health is the leading digital platform for durable medical equipment (DME), home medical equipment, and medical supply ePrescribing. Clinicians eSign and submit DME orders in seconds, and the platform coordinates in real time across a network of 3,000+ supplier locations, 270,000+ eSigning clinicians, and 70,000+ facilities in all 50 states. Parachute integrates with EHR/EMR systems (athenahealth, PointClickCare, Epic, and others) using HL7 2.x and FHIR interfaces, and offers prior-authorization automation, health-plan workflows, and value-based-care coordination. Integration is delivered as private, partner-provisioned EMR/HL7/FHIR interfaces rather than a public self-service developer API.

companies.name: Aware Health
companies.description: Aware Health is an AI-powered musculoskeletal (MSK) care platform that helps employers, health plans, and brokers reduce MSK spend while preventing orthopedic surgeries and chronic pain. The company pairs licensed clinicians (physical therapists and health coaches) with an AI "Predict" engine to triage, navigate, and manage musculoskeletal conditions virtually, and reports reducing MSK costs by roughly 30%. Its platform spans MSK care, chronic care, surgery decision support, member navigation, analytics, and an employer dashboard, delivered via web and an iOS app. Aware Health is a Techstars portfolio company and has raised seed funding (including a $3M round led by Boomerang VC with Bright Ventures). This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Aware Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Cleerly
companies.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

companies.name: Equip Health
companies.description: Equip Health is a virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment provider founded in 2019 by Kristina Saffran and Erin Parks. Equip delivers 100% remote, insurance-covered care for all eating disorder diagnoses — anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), ARFID, atypical anorexia, and OSFED — using Family-Based Treatment (FBT) and other evidence-based approaches. Every patient is matched with a five-person care team: a therapist, medical provider, dietitian, family mentor, and peer mentor. Equip serves patients across the United States with no waitlist, publishes an extensive library of clinical and recovery articles, partners with providers and health plans, and operates a patient portal at my.equip.health. This profile catalogs Equip's public web, legal, security, and content surfaces; Equip publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program at this time.

companies.name: Halo Health (Symplr)
companies.description: Halo Health, now part of symplr and marketed as symplr Clinical Communications, is a HIPAA-compliant clinical communication and collaboration platform for healthcare organizations. It provides role-based secure messaging, voice communication, critical alert and clinical-alarm notification, and on-call schedule management so care teams can coordinate around patients. The platform integrates with hospital EHR and clinical systems using healthcare interoperability standards - HL7 ADT for patient admit/discharge/transfer events, HL7 ORU for laboratory and radiology results, and SMTP for alerts such as sepsis notifications - rather than through a documented public developer REST API. symplr acquired Halo Health to extend its healthcare operations software portfolio, and the product now sits alongside symplr's broader workforce, compliance, and provider-data solutions.

companies.name: Hello Heart
companies.description: Hello Heart is a digital health company that combines a mobile app, connected blood-pressure monitors, a smart pill box, and the Nia AI assistant (trained on ACC/AHA guidelines) to help people proactively manage cardiovascular health. Sold primarily to employers, health plans, unions, and public-sector benefits programs as a covered heart-health benefit, the platform pairs self-monitoring with clinically-grounded, "safe AI" coaching to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac risk. Hello Heart is HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type 2 audited, NIST CSF aligned, and HIPAA compliant, with data encrypted in transit and at rest and stored within U.S. borders. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture.

companies.name: Smile Digital Health
companies.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

companies.name: Machinify
companies.description: Machinify is an AI-powered healthcare payment integrity platform that streamlines and automates payment processes for health plans. Its products - Coordinate (claims coordination), Subrogate (subrogation management), Audit (payment audit), Pay (payment processing), and Pharmacy (pharmacy payment integrity) - run on a unified data layer that combines claims and medical records, healthcare foundation models trained on billions of data points, and task-specific AI agents with continuous-improvement feedback loops. Machinify reports 85+ customers including 18 of the top 20 US health plans, coverage of 270 million member lives, and more than $6B in annual cost avoidance and recoveries. The company is backed by Battery Ventures and GV. Machinify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference.

companies.name: Nitra
companies.description: Nitra is an integrated financial and operational platform — an "operating system" — for independent medical practices, unifying business banking, spend management, payments, accounting, capital, and front-desk automation in one system. Its core products include the Nitra Card (a Visa business card with cashback and vendor pricing), NitraMart (a medical-supplies marketplace), BillPay payment processing, accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Nextech), Trina (an AI assistant for phone reception and invoice matching), and capital products such as lending, equipment financing, and insurance factoring. Nitra primarily serves eye care, aesthetics, dental specialty, and fertility practices as well as multi-site groups. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA-aware, holds funds at FDIC-insured banks, and is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital. Nitra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Aidence
companies.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

companies.name: Attuned Intelligence
companies.description: Attuned Intelligence is a healthcare voice AI company that automates hospital and community health center call centers with supervised, EHR-integrated Voice AI Agents. Its agents answer every patient call instantly and in the caller's language, resolve needs end-to-end (appointment booking, medication refills, triage routing), and provide real-time human oversight with transcripts and reporting so automation stays safe and auditable. Founded in 2024 by leaders from DeepMind, Google Health, AssemblyAI, and DocuSign, the company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $13M in funding backed by Threshold Ventures, and serves customers including Cambridge Health Alliance and Lowell Community Health Center. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. Attuned publishes no first-party developer/product API; its Wix-hosted marketing site exposes a generic hosted Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content and business details.

companies.name: Basata
companies.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

companies.name: Patientdesk.ai
companies.description: Patientdesk.ai (Patientdesk AI, Inc.) is a California-based, Y Combinator-backed company building an AI-native operating system for dental practices. Its 24/7 AI phone receptionist handles inbound and outbound patient calls, appointment scheduling, real-time insurance verification during the call, automated payment collection and debt follow-up, intake, reminders, and lead generation. The product integrates directly with major dental practice management systems (Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, Curve Dental, and others) to book patients straight into a clinic's calendar. Patientdesk.ai is HIPAA compliant, follows SOC 2 security standards, supports multiple languages, and is offered on month-to-month contracts. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer/API surface (OpenAPI, docs, SDKs) is currently published; the company exposes a marketing site and a provider-authored llms.txt.

companies.name: RapidClaims
companies.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Virgo
companies.description: Virgo builds AI foundation models for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, targeting gut-mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Its flagship model, EndoDINO, was trained on the largest known endoscopy dataset (130,037 videos / ~3.5 billion frames), and EndoML is the GI-specific tooling environment for building clinical and research workflows on top of it. Virgo Cloud provides video capture and management for endoscopy procedures, while Virgo Trials accelerates clinical trials with automatic data capture, endoscopic scoring, placebo-response prediction, subgroup identification, and AI biomarker discovery. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Bevel
companies.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

companies.name: Foodvisor
companies.description: Foodvisor is a mobile nutrition platform whose Vision API uses computer vision and AI to identify food items from photographs and return nutritional information including calories, macronutrients, and serving estimates. The Vision API is offered to enterprise developers under a commercial agreement.

companies.name: Wheel
companies.description: Wheel is a healthcare technology company providing the infrastructure for modern telehealth. Its Wheel Horizon platform is a modular care-enablement system that combines a nationwide clinician network, evidence-based virtual care programs, and integrated clinical operations so digital health companies, health plans, retailers and pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations can launch and scale virtual care. Wheel also operates WheelX, an enterprise AI health exchange, and Connected Services for integration. Wheel exposes a partner API, governed by an API Terms of Use and gated behind an approval process; the platform is HIPAA compliant and maintains SOC 2 controls. Public API reference documentation, SDKs, and a developer portal are not published. Wheel was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV.

companies.description: Harris Ambulatory Care Enterprise (part of Harris Healthcare, a Harris Computer company) provides ambulatory healthcare software solutions including the Pulse electronic health record system. The platform supports a §170.315(g)(10) ONC certified FHIR API for third-party application developers to access patient data, provider information, and clinical resources. Pulse is deployed on-premises, so each provider hosts a separate API instance with its own base URL. Third-party developers must obtain an ONC 2015 Edition Certified API License and register with each provider organization.

companies.name: Metricwire
companies.description: Metricwire is a real-world data collection platform for ecological momentary assessment (EMA), experience sampling (ESM), and digital-health research. It helps organizations measure real-world experiences to inform treatments, service offerings, and policies. Researchers design studies, schedule time- and event-based prompts, collect participant self-reports alongside passive sensor and wearable data through native iOS and Android apps, and export the results for analysis. The platform is used across clinical trials, behavioral and public-health research, and patient-reported outcome programs, with an emphasis on data privacy and security (ISO 27001, GDPR). A production JSON API is served from api.metricwire.com and a participant/researcher application from app.metricwire.com, though Metricwire does not currently publish an open developer portal or machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: Accurx
companies.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

companies.name: Docura Health
companies.description: Docura Health builds purpose-built software for physicians who prepare medical-legal reports — independent medical examinations (IME), qualified medical examiner (QME), agreed medical examiner (AME), permanent-and-stationary, and supplemental evaluations. The platform organizes complete case files (medical records, audio, and video), generates intelligent chronological summaries that link back to source documents, guides AMA Guides-compliant impairment ratings (5th and 6th Edition), and produces structured reports from customizable templates matched to each evaluator's practice style. Docura is HIPAA compliant with enterprise-grade end-to-end encryption and audit trails, and is backed by Y Combinator. This profile was seeded from a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from Docura Health's public website and trust center; no public developer API or documentation was found at enrichment time.

companies.name: Life360
companies.description: Life360 is a family safety platform built around a location-sharing mobile app for iOS and Android, offering real-time member location, Place Alerts, location history, driving safety scores and trip history, crash detection, SOS alerts and emergency dispatch, plus digital safety features such as identity theft protection and dark web monitoring. Its hardware line, following the acquisitions of Tile and Jiobit, spans Tile Mate, Pro, Slim and Sticker Bluetooth item trackers and a cellular GPS pet tracker, sold direct and through Amazon, Best Buy, Target and Walmart. The service is sold as Free, Silver, Gold and Platinum membership tiers. Life360 publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is an agent-facing one (llms.txt, an ai-plugin manifest whose advertised OpenAPI does not resolve, and Content-Signal directives in robots.txt). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

companies.name: Mon Ami

Mon Ami serves state units on aging, area agencies on aging, intellectual and developmental disabilities programs, Medicaid HCBS providers, and ombudsman programs, helping them reduce administrative burden while improving outcome documentation and compliance reporting. The platform references HL7/FHIR interoperability with EHRs, managed care organizations, and state systems. Mon Ami is a Felicis portfolio company; it does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time.

Its enterprise and partner integration surface is delivered through a gated developer portal (developers.wheel.com) rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; the "Wheel 3" name is a portfolio-scrape artifact for Wheel (wheel.com), which also appears in the network as the `wheel` stub (backed by CRV).

Withings announced the discontinuation of the standalone 8fit app effective June 26, 2026, folding its nutrition and activity content into the Withings app and Withings+ service. 8fit is a mobile/web consumer app and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

AISight Link is a partner-integration API without a public self-serve developer portal; access is arranged through PathAI (digitaldx@pathai.com).

Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, whose Stanford work produced one of the first retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for clinical medicine, the platform consolidates the medical AI ecosystem into a single interface where healthcare workers reach a library of medical AI tools through an integrated LLM assistant. It is designed to run inside existing electronic health record (EHR) systems, operate under institutional governance and controls, and stay grounded in peer-reviewed evidence rather than unverified data or pharmaceutical advertising. Almanac Health raised a $10M seed round in April 2026 led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst (which led the pre-seed) and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

companies.name: RealWear
companies.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

Aquant integrates with existing CRM and field-service systems and continuously learns from an organization's institutional service knowledge to drive service revenue, scale service teams, accelerate onboarding, and increase remote resolution rates. Aquant is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. The platform includes the ZioSuite clinician portal for report interpretation and patient management, the MyZio patient app for symptom logging and education, EHR integration, and telehealth workflows. iRhythm was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. companies.name: Omni Network
companies.description: Omni Network is a crypto interoperability protocol that makes the entire multi-chain ecosystem feel like a single chain for users and developers. Its core product, SolverNet, is a network of solvers that fulfill cross-chain intents on a user's behalf, letting a dApp deployed on one chain be used by people whose funds live on another. Developers integrate SolverNet through the Omni SDK (the @omni-network/core and @omni-network/react TypeScript packages) to bridge, swap, deposit, and bundle arbitrary contract calls across any supported chain from a single frontend. The project is built on a Go/Cosmos-SDK monorepo with Solidity contracts and ships the OMNI ERC-20 token on Ethereum L1. In 2026 the company rebranded from Omni to Nomina, consolidated on Ethereum, and now also operates Nomina, a unified trading terminal for power users trading perpetual futures across decentralized exchanges. It is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, Two Sigma, Spartan Group, and Vessel.

companies.description: Swift Medical develops AI-powered wound and skin care management software for healthcare organizations across acute, post-acute, home health, and hospice settings. Its flagship Skin & Wound app captures calibrated wound images on mobile devices, applies computer-vision tissue analytics and auto-tracing to measure and classify wounds, and coordinates care through longitudinal documentation backed by the company's database of more than 32 million wound images. The platform emphasizes secure, compliant handling of protected health information (SOC 2 Type 2, encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, MFA) and single sign-on via Okta and Microsoft. Swift Medical does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through direct engagement and enterprise SSO/EHR arrangements. companies.name: Framewise Health
companies.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. It then tracks patient comprehension in real time, giving care teams engagement data to flag which patients need follow-up. Framewise integrates with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), Athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks, and NextGen, and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant with an AWS BAA and end-to-end encryption. It targets hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and private clinics seeking to improve patient outcomes and medication adherence.

companies.description: Hormona is a women's hormonal-health company founded in 2020 by Karolina Lofqvist and Jasmine Tagesson, with offices in London, UK and Stockholm, Sweden. It builds a hormone-tracking mobile app together with an at-home hormone monitor and urine-test kits that users scan with a phone camera to get real-time, quantitative hormone results without a lab visit. Pear Suite reports serving 2,500+ community workers across 300+ organizations nationwide.

Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. companies.name: Faks

companies.name: Juli
companies.description: Juli is a US-based (Hull, Massachusetts) digital-health company building an AI-powered mobile platform that helps people manage complex, hard-to-treat chronic conditions — including asthma, migraine, depression, and bipolar disorder.
