Juli's efficacy has been evaluated in two randomized controlled trials (asthma and depression), published in JMIR and a SAGE journal, and the company reports retention far above consumer-health norms. Founded by Bettina Duehrkoop, Juli raised a $3.8M seed round in March 2022 co-led by Speedinvest and Norrsken VC. It serves consumers directly plus provider, employer, education (juli.education), pharma, and research (juli.science) channels. Pricing is performance based (1.5% of net collections recovered, nothing upfront). LunaBill is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type I (Type II in progress). It does not currently publish a public developer API; integration is delivered through EHR and clearinghouse connectors rather than a documented API surface.

companies.name: ABILITY Network (Inovalon)
companies.description: ABILITY Network is a healthcare SaaS business acquired by Inovalon in 2018 and now delivered as part of the cloud-based Inovalon ONE Platform. It provides US healthcare providers with software for medical billing and claims management, eligibility verification, revenue cycle management, clinical quality reporting, patient access, and workforce/staffing and care coordination. Inovalon pairs these provider-facing applications with large national datasets and analytics to support data-driven healthcare across payers, providers, pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations. Developer access to Inovalon ONE APIs is offered through the authenticated Inovalon developer portal at developer.inovalonone.com, which exposes sandbox, staging, and live environments.

companies.name: Circle Medical
companies.description: Circle Medical is a San Francisco-based online and in-person primary care clinic offering telemedicine and clinic-based visits with same and next-day availability. Founded through Y Combinator, the company operates 20+ physical locations and provides virtual appointments across multiple US states through Circle Medical Care of California, an independent medical practice. Its 400+ board-certified physicians, physician assistants, and nurse practitioners treat primary care, mental health (ADHD, anxiety, depression), hormone and sexual health, urgent care, weight loss (GLP-1s), sleep, and dermatology. Circle Medical is a HIPAA-covered, patient-facing digital health provider; it publishes no public developer API or SDK program, and this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: kelaHealth
companies.description: kelaHealth is a healthcare AI company that improves surgical outcomes through its Surgical Intelligence Service, an AI-enabled API delivering patient-specific predictive insights at critical decision points across the perioperative process. Models trained on millions of surgical procedures predict individual patient risk across nine major complication categories, identify modifiable factors, and recommend stratified interventions tailored to hospital standards. The service integrates into existing medtech and healthcare software applications using EHR, robotic, and social-determinants-of-health data to help providers improve growth, efficiency, quality, and safety. kelaHealth is HIPAA compliant and backed by Techstars. It does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its API is delivered through partner integrations.

companies.name: Ultromics
companies.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Calo
companies.description: Calo is a food-tech company founded in Bahrain in 2019 that operates a personalized meal-subscription and delivery service. Nutritionist-designed, chef-prepared meals are portioned to each customer's health goals and lifestyle, with 80+ new meal options rotated weekly and flexible pause/cancel anytime. Built by chefs, nutritionists, and software engineers around proprietary nutritional algorithms, Calo has expanded to seven markets across the GCC and beyond (Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman), ordered through its consumer apps. Calo is backed by 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documented client SDKs.

companies.name: LifeSite
companies.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

companies.name: Medzoomer
companies.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: AvoMD
companies.description: AvoMD (Avo) is a clinical AI platform that integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) systems to power AI copilots for healthcare workflows. It combines EHR data with trusted clinical knowledge bases to support decision-making, documentation, and care delivery across inpatient and outpatient settings. Avo's product line includes Chart Assist, an AI Scribe for ambient clinical documentation, and AI Consult, serving rural and small hospitals, large and mid-size hospitals, and ambulatory care, in partnership with medical societies and knowledge partners. The company is SOC 2 Type II compliant and backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: TherapyNotes
companies.description: TherapyNotes is a HIPAA-compliant practice management and electronic health record (EHR) platform built specifically for behavioral health - therapists, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, and group practices. It provides interactive note templates and clinical documentation, scheduling with appointment reminders, a client portal, telehealth, electronic insurance claims and ERA, credit card processing, and TherapyFuel AI tooling. As of this writing TherapyNotes does NOT expose a public or partner developer API, webhooks, or documented programmatic interface; access to client, appointment, clinical-note, and billing data is through the browser application and manual exports only. This entry documents TherapyNotes as an API-relevant provider and honestly models the capability areas a behavioral-health EHR API would cover; the API surfaces below are modeled, not published, and no endpoints are fabricated.

companies.name: Virgin Pulse
companies.description: Virgin Pulse is a corporate health and employee wellbeing platform that in 2024 merged with HealthComp and rebranded as Personify Health, operating today at personifyhealth.com. The company delivers a personalized health platform that unites wellbeing, healthcare navigation and advocacy, benefits administration, third-party administration (TPA), and rewards into a single employee experience for enterprises, health plans, and health systems. Integration with Personify Health is handled through an authentication-gated developer portal (developer.personifyhealth.com) and a partner marketplace (marketplace.personifyhealth.com); there is no publicly documented, open API specification. This profile was seeded as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched from the company's live public surface (llms.txt, status page, developer portal, and DNS/TLS probes).

companies.name: Doctronic
companies.description: Doctronic is a consumer telemedicine platform that pairs an AI doctor with licensed physicians for anonymous, low-cost health care. Users describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that performs a free symptom assessment and health consultation, then can escalate to a real doctor for a video visit ($39/visit), prescription refills, lab orders, and follow-up care. Positioned as "Free. Anonymous. Built by doctors," the product is direct-to-consumer web and mobile rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The only public machine-readable surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

companies.name: Modern Fertility
companies.description: Modern Fertility is a women's health company offering at-home fertility and hormone testing along with pregnancy, ovulation and prenatal products. Its flagship Modern Fertility Hormone Test lets people measure reproductive hormones from home and review results with providers. The company was acquired by telehealth provider Ro and is now operated as part of Ro: modernfertility.com redirects to ro.co/fertility and the brand's products, accounts, legal terms and security program are served under the parent Ro platform. Modern Fertility exposes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a consumer health brand within the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Paradigm Health
companies.description: Paradigm Health is an AI-native clinical trial platform connecting biopharma sponsors with a research-ready provider network spanning roughly 2,100 care locations across the United States. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, the company operates infrastructure implemented at healthcare provider organizations to make clinical research part of routine care. Its Study Conduct platform captures data directly from electronic health records and other structured and unstructured sources, algorithmically evaluates FDA-defined data points in real time, and transmits the critical safety and efficacy signals needed for regulatory determinations to trial sponsors and the FDA. Paradigm serves both trial sponsors (protocol optimization, feasibility and site selection, patient identification and enrollment, data collection and delivery, post-approval evidence) and research sites. The company acquired Flatiron Health's Clinical Research business, announced a research collaboration with the U.S. FDA, and is backed by ARCH Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and GV. Paradigm currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity, legal, and published security/compliance surface.

companies.name: Pharmeasy
companies.description: PharmEasy is one of India's largest digital healthcare platforms, operating a consumer online pharmacy and health marketplace at pharmeasy.in. It lets users order prescription and over-the-counter medicines (with prescription upload and verification), buy health and wellness products, book diagnostic lab tests and health checkup packages, and consult doctors via telemedicine, plus a PLUS subscription for recurring savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. PharmEasy runs an internal API at api.pharmeasy.in but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it does operate a responsible-disclosure security program (infosec@pharmeasy.in). Sector: healthcare / e-pharmacy.

companies.name: Sage Care
companies.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

companies.name: Asepha
companies.description: Asepha is an AI workflow automation platform built specifically for pharmacies, positioning itself as "the context graph for the therapy-start journey" with a stated vision to make medication delays impossible. Its AI agents automate repetitive pharmacy operations across automated prescription data entry, back-office work, 340B management (TPA matching, accruals, purchase-order automation), medication reconciliation (Best Possible Medication History), a conversational voice call assistant, benefits verification and prior-authorization (BV/PA) automation, REMS compliance reporting, and medication therapy review. The company reports outcomes such as a 32% reduction in manual labour cost within one month and tasks completed 4x faster than baseline. Asepha is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, with AES-256 encryption at rest. Founded by CEO Eunice Wu, PharmD and CTO Can Uncu, the company operates from New York, NY and Toronto, ON, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Asepha publishes no public API, developer portal, or specifications at this time.

companies.name: Joyful
companies.description: Joyful Health provides AI-assisted revenue recovery for healthcare organizations, combining automated claim investigation with expert billing teams to recover unpaid and denied insurance claims. Its platform runs inside an organization's existing revenue-cycle-management (RCM) systems rather than replacing them, covering denial investigation and root-cause analysis, claims recovery and appeals management, historical accounts-receivable (A/R) assessment, payer follow-up, documentation review, and financial insight to prevent future denials. The company operates a customer application at app.joyfulhealth.io and maintains a Vanta-hosted trust center. Joyful is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; Joyful does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

companies.name: myLaurel
companies.description: myLaurel is a New York-based healthcare company delivering acute and transitional care in patients' homes. Its hybrid model pairs hands-on clinical teams with virtual technology support to prevent unnecessary hospitalizations, free critical hospital bed space, improve patient outcomes, and lower the total cost of care for both health systems and health plans. Reported results include a 49% reduction in 30-day readmissions, an average 1.5-day length-of-stay reduction, a 97 Net Promoter Score, and 3:1+ ROI within 90 days. myLaurel is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This profile has been enriched from the company's public web surface; it currently exposes no public developer API.

companies.name: Qventus
companies.description: Qventus is a healthcare technology company that provides an AI-powered automation platform for hospital operations. Its "AI teammates" combine machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to streamline care-coordination workflows across surgical growth and operating-room utilization, perioperative and pre-admission-testing coordination, inpatient capacity and discharge planning, and care-gap and coding automation. Qventus sells to health systems and hospitals as a B2B SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Mayfield, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

companies.name: SAVA
companies.description: SAVA (sava.health) is a health-monitoring company developing a minimally invasive, continuous multi-molecule biosensor worn just beneath the skin. The platform is designed to capture real-time molecular data - glucose, lactate, ketones, sodium, histamine, urea, alcohol, and cortisol - and surface it through a connected mobile app, aiming to shift healthcare toward preventative monitoring and personal wellness. The company is early stage and pre-launch, operating a waiting-list model for early access to its device rather than a public product. It publishes no first-party developer API or health-data API; its marketing site is built on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint and a published llms.txt for agentic access to public site content only. Backed by Balderton Capital.

companies.name: Bold
companies.description: Bold (Age Bold, Inc.) is an AI-enabled healthy-aging company founded in 2019 by Amanda Rees and Hari Arul that combines age-friendly virtual care with senior-focused exercise and nutrition programs for Medicare members. The platform delivers personalized at-home programs — live and on-demand classes, balance and fall-prevention regimens, pain and mobility programs, nutrition coaching, and telehealth visits with clinicians — to adults 65 and older, distributed through Medicare Advantage plans, provider groups, and the CMS ACCESS program rather than sold as a developer platform. Bold reports its balance programs lower fall risk and its pain programs reduce joint pain among participating members, and states its platform is HIPAA compliant and requires no lengthy IT integration for plan partners. The company has raised roughly $27M, with a $17M Series A led by Rethink Impact alongside Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health, Khosla Ventures, Samsung Next, GingerBread Capital, and Primetime Partners. As of this enrichment pass Bold publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or partner API surface — integrations are handled through its partnerships team.

companies.name: BrightInsight
companies.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.

companies.name: Curative
companies.description: Curative is a health insurance and healthcare services company founded in 2020 that reengineered the employer-based health plan around simplicity, engagement, and cost transparency. Its fully insured and level-funded plans give members a competitive monthly premium with zero copays, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs, starting each member with a baseline visit that tailors a preventative care plan. Curative serves more than 1,200 employer clients and over 165,000 members, reached profitability, and achieved unicorn status ($1.275B valuation) following a $150M Series B round backed by DCVC. Curative operates as a HIPAA-regulated health plan; it has no public developer/API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, its member/provider web surface, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Dorsata
companies.description: Dorsata is a women's health technology company based in Arlington, Virginia that reimagines the electronic health record (EHR) experience for obstetrics and gynecology providers, life sciences, and health plans. Its flagship Dorsata Prenatal platform overlays a practice's existing EHR with an ACOG-aligned prenatal flowsheet and a clinical rules engine that surfaces the right guidance at the right point of care, improving diagnosis, treatment, and documentation while reducing physician burnout. Additional products include Dorsata Insights, which gathers standardized real-world clinical data from women's health providers (including populations historically underrepresented in clinical studies), Dorsata Pathways, and an Adnexal Mass solution. The platform serves 300+ practice sites and thousands of clinical users across roughly 20 states, documenting hundreds of thousands of pregnancies. Dorsata raised a $5.2M Series A with participation from QED Investors, Women's Health USA, LabCorp, Fool Ventures, and Gore Range Capital. This API Evangelist profile tracks Dorsata as a healthtech company; the company exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Lantum
companies.description: Lantum (formerly Network Locum, founded 2012 in Shoreditch, London) is a United Kingdom healthcare workforce-management company whose Connected Scheduling platform helps NHS primary- and secondary-care organisations build digital staff banks, manage rotas and e-rostering, run automated timesheets and payments, and fill clinical shifts from a verified network of 30,000+ locum clinicians. It serves over 2,000 primary-care organisations, GP practices, PCNs, GP federations, and integrated care systems across the UK. Lantum is a practice-management and workforce platform rather than a clinical-data interoperability vendor, and it does NOT publish a public developer portal, a documented REST API, or an HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement. Its product is delivered through a gated web and mobile application (lantum.com), onboarded via sales and demo request, with any system integrations (for example to GP clinical systems) handled through private partner arrangements rather than a self-serve public API.

companies.name: Ophelia

Founded in 2020 and based in Philadelphia, Ophelia combines evidence-based buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone) prescriptions with virtual clinical care, delivering diagnosis, prescriptions sent to local pharmacies, ongoing clinician support, and insurance coordination entirely remotely. Patients can be seen within 1-3 days and most pay under $10/month. Ophelia is a consumer-facing healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

companies.name: Prosper Health
companies.description: Prosper Health is a telehealth provider focused exclusively on autistic and neurodivergent adults, offering virtual autism diagnostic assessments and ongoing affirming, strength-based therapy delivered by licensed psychologists and therapists who specialize in adult autism. Its adult-validated, telehealth-native assessment (an alternative to the child-oriented ADOS) runs entirely online across two psychologist sessions plus a feedback session, with results reported within roughly two weeks. Prosper Health accepts major insurers (Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, Oscar, Oxford, United) across 20-plus US states. It is a direct-to-consumer clinical care company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its web, security, and identity properties for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Spring Health
companies.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

companies.name: Stellar Sleep
companies.description: Stellar Sleep (Y Combinator S23, backed by Initialized Capital) is a mobile app that helps people with chronic insomnia sleep better using psychology rather than medication. Its personalized program is based on CBT-I (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia), the first-line treatment recommended by sleep experts, delivered through iOS and Android apps published by Merlin Collective, LLC. Started at Harvard Innovation Labs in 2021, Stellar Sleep also offers clinician and employer programs, with clinical-system integrations arranged by its team. It is a consumer digital-health product with no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface.

companies.name: WellTheory
companies.description: WellTheory is a virtual autoimmune care platform that provides whole-person support for people living with autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, pairing members with a dedicated care team for nutrition, lifestyle, and clinical guidance across more than 100 conditions. The company sells to employers and health plans as a covered benefit as well as direct to consumers, and is backed by Accel and General Catalyst. WellTheory publishes no public developer API surface today; its api.welltheory.com backend and docs are private/internal.

companies.name: Ambiq Micro
companies.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

companies.name: Kheiron Medical Technologies
companies.description: Kheiron Medical Technologies is a London-founded medical-imaging AI company best known for Mia (Mammography Intelligent Assessment), a deep-learning solution that supports radiologists in breast-cancer screening as an independent, concurrent, or triage reader. Founded in 2016 and backed by investors including Atomico, Kheiron now operates as part of RadNet's DeepHealth, whose portfolio spans breast, prostate, lung, brain, and thyroid imaging plus the Diagnostic, Operations, and TechLive suites. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kheiron/DeepHealth as a health-AI provider; the company exposes clinical products and enterprise integrations rather than a public self-serve developer API, so most machine-readable API artifacts are not applicable and this record captures its identity, security, and legal surface.

companies.name: Ro
companies.description: Ro (ro.co) is a direct-to-consumer telehealth company that connects patients with US-licensed healthcare providers entirely online, offering prescription treatment, provider visits, and pharmacy fulfillment across categories including men's and women's health, weight management (Ro Body), dermatology (Ro Derm), hair loss, fertility (Ro Fertility), and sexual health. Ro deliberately operates a "Zero-API" vertically integrated online-visit experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; its only public machine-readable surface is a security posture (RFC 9116 security.txt and a HackerOne vulnerability disclosure program). Ro is backed by Canaan Partners, General Catalyst, and Initialized Capital.

companies.name: Tasso
companies.description: Tasso, Inc. designs painless, needle-free blood collection devices and an end-to-end logistics platform for decentralized and at-home blood sampling. Its product line includes Tasso+ for capillary whole-blood collection, the Tasso-M20/Mini for dried blood microsampling, and the tile-T20 for liquid serum and plasma, enabling remote specimen collection for clinical trials, patient screening, diagnostics, and research. Tasso pairs the hardware with kitting, shipping, and sample-return logistics and is cited in over 100 peer-reviewed publications. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Min Doktor
companies.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

companies.name: Tennr
companies.description: Tennr is a New York City-based healthcare technology company (founded 2021) building agentic patient-orchestration software that automates referral-based care operations for providers and health systems. Its proprietary vision-language model, RaeLM, is trained on over 100 million anonymized medical documents to read faxes, referrals, and unstructured records, then automates document classification, data extraction, patient qualification, insurance eligibility verification, and prior-authorization submission by integrating directly with existing EHR systems. Tennr processes over 10 million documents monthly and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant. It raised a $101M Series C at a $605M valuation led by IVP, with a16z, Lightspeed, GV, ICONIQ, and Foundation Capital participating. Tennr does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or specification; integrations are delivered through EHR connections and professional services.

companies.name: ThinkSono
companies.description: ThinkSono is a medical technology company that develops AI-powered ultrasound software enabling non-specialist clinicians to detect deep vein thrombosis (DVT) blood clots at the point of care. Its real-time AI guidance walks a clinician through capturing and interpreting a compression ultrasound scan, compressing what is typically a full-day specialist referral pathway into an approximately 30-minute point-of-care assessment. The product is positioned for hospital and primary-care settings (including NHS deployments) to reduce DVT diagnostic waiting times. ThinkSono is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. It is a B2B medical-device software business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: 23andMe
companies.description: 23andMe is a consumer genetics and biotechnology company founded in 2006 that sells saliva-based DNA test kits and returns ancestry composition, DNA relative matching, genetic health-predisposition and carrier-status reports, wellness and trait insights, and pharmacogenetic results directly to consumers, alongside a research arm that studies aggregated, consented genetic data. 23andMe historically published a scope-gated, OAuth 2.0 Personal Genome API at api.23andme.com, but closed third-party developer API access in September 2018; the company entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025 and its consumer web presence and assets have since shifted to the 23andme.org domain. No public, live developer API surface remains, though the company maintains a trust center and a security disclosure program.

companies.name: 7 Cups
companies.description: 7 Cups (7cups.com) is an on-demand emotional health and online therapy service founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator. It connects people seeking support with a network of trained volunteer listeners for free, anonymous one-on-one chat, and matches members with licensed therapists and social workers for paid online therapy delivered by messaging, audio, or video. The platform also runs peer community forums, group support chat rooms, and self-help "growth path" content. 7 Cups operates across 189 countries in 140 languages with hundreds of thousands of trained listeners. It is a consumer web and mobile product rather than an API-first developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and carries no public API at this time.

companies.name: Cortico
companies.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.

companies.name: Curve Dental
companies.description: Curve Dental is a cloud-based, all-in-one dental practice management software company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia. Curve is privately held and backed by Battery Ventures, and connects to a growing ecosystem of integration partners (including DentalXChange, DentalHQ, Pearl AI, Bola AI, and Mango Voice) rather than exposing a public self-serve developer API. This profile was seeded from Battery Ventures' portfolio and enriched from Curve Dental's public web surface; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

The platform pairs an in-house clinical team with education and training, diagnostics and testing, prescriptions and medication delivery, and financing/reimbursement, delivered to staff through a mobile app and to HR teams through enterprise and SME plans. Fertifa is London-based, backed by Speedinvest, and works with employers including Lululemon, Meta, Bain Capital, and Virgin. companies.name: LUMICKS
companies.description: LUMICKS is a life-science instrumentation company that builds tools to directly measure molecular and cellular interactions. Its Dynamic Single-Molecule platform, the C-Trap, uses optical tweezers to resolve real-time biomolecular interactions at the single-molecule level, while its Cell Avidity platforms (Avidion and the compact z-Movi) quantify the binding strength between immune cells and their targets for immuno-oncology, CAR-T, and antibody-therapeutics research. The developer surface is client-side: the official Apache-2.0 Python library lumicks.pylake analyzes single-molecule optical-tweezer data exported from the Bluelake acquisition software (force calibration, force-distance curve fitting, kymo/scan imaging, kymotracking, population dynamics), and bluelake-scripting automates instrument control. LUMICKS publishes no hosted public web API.

Operating as a telehealth platform contracted with employers and health plans, Pomelo pairs licensed clinicians, doulas, and care teams with remote monitoring to close the gaps between doctor visits, reduce NICU admissions, and improve maternal and infant outcomes. The company reports covering 25 million lives across all 50 states and raised a $92M Series C at a $1.7B valuation. Pomelo Care is a patient-, employer-, and payer-facing platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and First Round Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and monitoring.

companies.name: Bristle
companies.description: Bristle (Bristle Health) is a consumer health company that makes the world's first at-home oral microbiome saliva test, helping people measure, understand, and improve their oral health. companies.description: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is a global Fortune 500 biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and delivering innovative medicines for patients with serious diseases. BMS focuses on oncology, immunology, cardiovascular, fibrosis, and cell therapy (CAR T). The company operates BMS Study Connect for clinical trial recruitment, a Medical Information portal for healthcare providers, and the BMS Business Development platform for research partnerships and data sharing. companies.name: C the Signs
companies.description: C the Signs is a London-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016 by Dr Bea Bakshi and Dr Miles Payling, that uses artificial intelligence to help clinicians detect and refer patients at risk of cancer at the earliest, most treatable stage. Registered as an MHRA Class I medical device, its clinical decision support platform analyzes more than 1,000 validated, evidence-based data points across signs, symptoms and risk factors to recommend the right investigations or urgent referrals in under 60 seconds. The platform is used widely across the UK's NHS and health systems, has helped identify over 70,000 patients with cancer across 100+ cancer types at reported 99% sensitivity, and is backed by an $8M Series A investment from Khosla Ventures. It has no public developer API; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network lead.

Its products include 1:1 direct messaging, appointment lifecycle messaging, population outreach, health coaching, closed-loop referrals, Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) workflows, and Wellness Copilot, an AI-backed diabetes-management automation. CareMessage does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; access to the platform is through its web application and a login-gated help center. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from CareMessage's public web surface.

companies.name: Eleos Health
companies.description: Eleos Health is the most widely adopted AI platform in behavioral and community-based healthcare. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, Eleos delivers purpose-built AI workflow agents that span clinical documentation, compliance, and revenue cycle management. The platform embeds directly inside providers' existing web-based electronic health records (EHRs) via a lightweight browser extension for both in-person and telehealth sessions, turning ambient session capture or quick text summaries into structured, payer-ready progress notes and cutting documentation time by roughly 70%. Eleos Compliance reviews every note against common risk areas (note cloning, empty notes, interventions, progress mentions, action plans, and the golden thread), and its revenue cycle tooling automates eligibility checks and claim protection. Deployed across 120+ care organizations in 30+ states, Eleos integrates without custom API builds; it is backed by Menlo Ventures and Greenfield Partners.

Ennoble Care is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Its technology turns the microphone in an ordinary smartphone into a screening device, analyzing audio to detect signs of heart, breathing, brain, and gut conditions at a standard targeting in-clinic specialist examinations. DFI's first commercial product, Sonus Health, is a veterinary heart-screening platform: clinics and pet owners record 30 seconds of heart sound from dogs (cats and horses coming soon) with a phone, and AI returns heart rate, heart rate variability, murmur detection, and a composite Heart Health Score in seconds, with a full report reviewed by a board-certified veterinary cardiologist within 48 hours. Sonus Health ships as iOS and Android apps for pet owners and a web dashboard for veterinary clinics.

companies.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

companies.name: Spill
companies.description: Spill is a UK-based employee assistance programme (EAP) that delivers mental health support to employees directly inside the tools teams already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform offers same-day, message-based counselling, structured multi-session therapy courses for specific mental health conditions, drop-in group sessions, manager mental-health training, and self-guided wellbeing content, all through a single subscription. Spill serves over 600 companies on month-to-month terms and is backed by Seedcamp. It is a B2B software-as-a-service wellbeing product rather than an API provider; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been published.

companies.description: Accolade is a personalized healthcare and benefits navigation platform for employers and health plans. It pairs members with a care team of advocates, registered nurses, physicians, and mental-health specialists to help them understand their benefits, find in-network care, book appointments, and manage chronic and complex conditions. Accolade combines this human advocacy with virtual primary care, expert medical opinion, and mental-health services delivered through its member web and mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Accolade is a member-facing benefits platform and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

It is a LegitScript-certified healthcare merchant that sources directly from manufacturers and distributors, with qualified pharmacists handling procurement, storage, and dispensing. Dawaai is backed by 500 Global and operates across Pakistan, including Karachi and Rawalpindi. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network via the venture portfolio pipeline; Dawaai publishes no public developer/API program at this time.

companies.name: Finni Health
companies.description: Finni Health is a telehealth company that connects families of children on the autism spectrum with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapists and mental health providers. Operating across more than 30 states, Finni offers both in-home and in-clinic ABA therapy with flexible scheduling, handles insurance coordination and billing for its provider network, and gives parents a portal for progress tracking and family-led goal setting. The company positions itself as an operating platform for ABA practices as well as a care provider for families, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

companies.name: Five Lives
companies.description: Five Lives is a health-technology company building evidence-based digital tools for dementia prevention and brain health for adults aged 50 and over. Founded by former Peak brain-training leaders Xavier Louis (CEO) and Sylvain Piquet (COO), the fully remote company operates two consumer mobile apps: Five Lives Brain Health, a prevention app available since 2021 with cognitive tests, brain games, and lifestyle tracking across five pillars (nutrition, sleep, physical activity, mood and social connection, and mental stimulation); and Five Lives Care, an evidence-based memory and autonomy programme for people aged 60+ launched in January 2026 and developed with leading memory centres in the UK and France. Its work draws on the FINGER study and the Lancet Commission's modifiable dementia risk factors, with research partners including the University of Oxford, Trinity College Dublin, the FINGER Brain Health Institute, Dementias Platform UK, and the Gerontopole d'Ile de France. Backed by Speedinvest. Five Lives does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Frontera
companies.description: Frontera (Frontera Health) is an AI-assisted clinical documentation company for behavioral health. Its software automates assessment and diagnosis report writing for Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and clinical psychologists working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and autism care, cutting report time from 6-10 hours to 2-3 hours. The platform pairs a BCBA-trained AI Assessment Builder and Diagnosis Builder with digital phenotyping, and is delivered as a HIPAA-compliant web application (customer login at portal.fronterahealth.com) rather than a public API. Frontera is a venture-backed portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and security surface; as of this pass Frontera publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server.

companies.description: Milu Health is a health technology company that pairs a virtual care team with an AI engine to help employees and their families get higher-quality healthcare at a lower cost. Founded in 2023 by Sasha Gribov and Gautam Kumar, Milu integrates directly with electronic health record (EHR) data from tens of thousands of provider groups and health systems to proactively flag medication issues, care gaps, fairly priced and high-quality doctors, incorrect medical bills, and more affordable medications. The platform also ingests an employer's health plan and benefits so it can notify members when an existing benefit could help. Milu is offered through employers and benefits advisors as well as directly to individuals. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by a16z Bio + Health in March 2024. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; Milu does not currently publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Poppins
companies.description: Poppins is a French digital health company that develops a clinically validated digital therapeutic (DTx) for children aged 7-11 with dyslexia. Classified as a Class I medical device under EU Regulation 2017/745, the mobile application delivers home-based, game-based training sessions of about 20 minutes per day, 3-5 times per week, targeting phonological awareness, reading speed, and visual attention span. Poppins complements in-person speech therapy, supports speech-language pathologists through professional accounts, and partners with insurers. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Poppins publishes a consumer and healthcare-professional web/mobile product but no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

companies.name: Q Bio
companies.description: Q Bio is a Redwood City, California health-technology company offering the Q Exam and the Q Bio Health Dashboard, sold directly at its clinic and through enterprise partners. The Q Exam is a comprehensive preventive-health assessment that combines whole-body non-contrast MRI, 120+ blood biomarkers, analysis of 163 risk-relevant genes, wearable data, medical history, and board-certified physician review into a single longitudinal health baseline. Imaging is quantified by Constellation, the company's FDA-cleared AI image-analysis software that segments organs and measures anatomy, and results are stored in the Q Bio Health Dashboard for year-over-year comparison. Q Bio is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.

The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. companies.description: AlemHealth is an AI-powered teleradiology and medical imaging platform that unifies image acquisition, diagnostic reading, reporting, and analytics into a single cloud system used by 500+ radiologists across 20+ countries. Its product suite includes Connect PACS (cloud image archiving with an FDA-approved diagnostic viewer), FrontDesk RIS scheduling, a referring-physician Referral Portal, a patient QR-access app, and the AlemBox gateway and AlemHub reporting-server hardware. AI features cover automated report drafting, quality-assurance scoring, laterality-mismatch detection, and ICD-10 tagging, metered via an AI-tokens model. For providers, AlemHealth supports bi-directional HL7, FHIR, and API integrations plus standard DICOM connectivity to sync orders, patient demographics, and finalized reports with existing EMR/EHR and PACS systems.

companies.name: Casana
companies.description: Casana (Casana Care) is a Rochester, New York digital-health company building passive, in-home remote patient monitoring hardware. Its flagship Smart Seat (formerly the Heart Seat) is a toilet-seat replacement that captures vital signs — heart rate, heart-rate variability, blood-oxygen (SpO2), respiration rate, blood-pressure insights, and sit-to-stand power — during normal bathroom use, with no wearables, no daily charging, and explicitly no camera or microphone. Readings sync to companion iOS, Android, and web apps for patients, families, and caregivers. The company operates in the digital health, remote patient monitoring, and connected medical-device space and is backed by General Catalyst and Kaiser Permanente. As of this profile Casana publishes a consumer product, companion apps, and legal/privacy pages, but no public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Medeloop
companies.description: Medeloop is an AI platform for the clinical research lifecycle, describing itself as an operating system for clinical research that spans grant discovery and funding, real-world evidence generation from patient data, and delivering actionable intelligence at the point of care. Its products include Medeloop Analytics (AI agents that analyze EHR, claims, and registry data without requiring users to code), EvidenceKit (analytics paired with all-payer claims data), Medeloop Grants (AI-assisted grant discovery and proposal writing), and Medeloop Care (population health and care management). The platform is federated (compute moves to the data, which stays in the customer's infrastructure), CDM-agnostic (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, OMOP, i2b2, or custom schemas), and model-agnostic (routing tasks across OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek), with multi-cloud deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premise. It serves pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, health systems, and clinical researchers. As of this enrichment pass Medeloop publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its documentation host (docs.medeloop.ai) is gated behind Okta authentication and its analytics application is a private client login.

companies.description: Aluna is a digital respiratory health company behind an FDA-cleared, portable Bluetooth spirometer and companion mobile app that let people with asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis measure lung function (FEV1) at home and share the results with their care teams. The platform pairs a hospital-grade sensor with a gamified app and machine-learning analytics to encourage proper technique, track symptoms, triggers, and medications, and surface trends that help clinicians intervene before an exacerbation. Founded by Charvi Shetty and Inderjit Jutla out of UC Berkeley's bioengineering program, Aluna raised a $15.3M Series B and is a Matrix Partners portfolio company; the product is now operated under Huma Therapeutics. Aluna publishes consumer, clinical-provider, and clinical-trial surfaces but no public developer API.

MTN OPS is a direct-to-consumer, internet-first retailer operating on the Shopify platform and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. companies.name: Amperos Health
companies.description: Amperos Health (Amperos) is an AI-native insurance revenue recovery platform for healthcare providers. It uses agentic AI together with experienced revenue cycle management (RCM) specialists to run the full insurance collections process, from claim submission through denial resolution to payment. The platform automates first-touch routine tasks, works complex denials with specialist oversight, and adapts configurable workflows to each organization's procedures across specialties including orthopedics, cardiology, behavioral health, DME/HME, ophthalmology, anesthesiology, dermatology, urology, dental, and oncology. Amperos reports outcomes such as higher claim recovery, reduced accounts receivable backlogs, and lower cost to collect for the healthcare providers it serves. The company is backed by Uncork Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company. Amperos currently exposes a marketing and demo-request surface rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public web properties and security posture.

AnswersNow accepts major insurance carriers including Medicaid, is BHCOE accredited and a CASP member organization, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. This profile has been enriched with company identity and domain-security posture; AnswersNow publishes a consumer web application (web.getanswersnow.com) but no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Curve Health

The platform unifies telemedicine, a health information exchange, predictive analytics, and smart billing into a single system so nurses, physicians, behavioral health providers, and facility operators can deliver care in place and reduce avoidable hospital transfers. Curve Health reports enabling 150,000+ remote care visits and an 80% reduction in hospitalizations for partner facilities, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Morningside. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web and product-documentation surface; Curve Health does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition.

Its core capabilities are privacy-preserving record linkage using Datavant tokens, HIPAA Expert Determination and de-identification, medical record retrieval / release of information, and real-world evidence generation for life sciences, payers, providers, and government. Datavant's integration surface is enterprise and partner/contract gated - an access-controlled API host exists at api.datavant.com (returns HTTP 403 to anonymous callers) but Datavant does not publish a self-serve public developer portal, a downloadable OpenAPI specification, or a FHIR CapabilityStatement. Home market is the United States.

It lets health systems scale best-practice care pathways across the enterprise so clinicians can focus on patients while operational cost falls and outcomes improve. Lumeon serves 70+ health systems globally — including Optum, NYC Health+Hospitals, and the NHS — and is now part of Health Catalyst. companies.name: MedHOK (Hearst Communications)
companies.description: MHK (formerly MedHOK), part of Hearst Health, is a healthcare technology company providing a unified SaaS platform for health plans and payers. Its CareProminence suite spans utilization management, care management, complaints/appeals and grievances, pharmacy management, population health and quality management, and interoperability (the MHK Interop Suite), while its MarketProminence suite covers enrollment and member maintenance, premium billing, financial reconciliation, and member web portals. MHK helps Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health plans streamline operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the member experience. The MHK Interop Suite supports FHIR, SMART on FHIR, Da Vinci, and CMS-0057 interoperability requirements. MHK publishes HITRUST and ISO 27001 certification and NCQA prevalidation. The company operates a public marketing and resource site but does not publish a public developer portal or API program.

companies.name: Myndlift
companies.description: Myndlift is a digital neurofeedback and mental-health company that pairs a consumer/clinical mobile app with a wearable EEG brain-sensing headband (Muse) to deliver therapist-guided, personalized brain-training programs. The platform provides brain mapping and assessments, gamified real-time neurofeedback sessions, progress tracking, and remote-monitoring dashboards used by both individuals and mental-health practitioners for attention, anxiety, stress, sleep, and peak-performance goals. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports 26,000+ members and more than one million neurofeedback sessions delivered. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record with verified identity links.

companies.name: OneHealthCompany
companies.description: The One Health Company is a Palo Alto veterinary precision-oncology company, best known for its FidoCure platform, that brings human-grade precision cancer medicine to dogs. FidoCure sequences a dog's tumor with next-generation DNA sequencing, matches the cancer-driving mutations to targeted therapies, and gives veterinarians an individualized treatment plan grounded in the world's largest proprietary canine cancer dataset (billions of data points across a network of more than 1,300 veterinary clinics). The company was founded in 2015 by Christina Lopes and Ben Lewis on the "One Health" thesis that treating cancer in companion dogs also advances real-world evidence for human oncology. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z bio), Y Combinator, Polaris Partners, Borealis Ventures, Lerer Hippeau and Tau Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer and veterinarian web experience (including a veterinarian login portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

companies.name: Pathai
companies.description: PathAI is a healthcare artificial-intelligence company transforming pathology through machine learning. Its AISight Image Management System (IMS) and the AISight Link open API deliver AI-assisted disease detection, biomarker quantification, fields-of-interest and AI Impressions, and laboratory workflow integration for pathologists, hospital and reference labs, and biopharma research partners. AISight Link is an enterprise interoperability surface that connects AISight with third-party AI algorithms and Laboratory Information Systems (LIS/LIMS) over REST and HL7; PathAI does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. The company is ISO 27001 certified and operates a vulnerability disclosure program. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc.

Its consumer products - including Glucose Control, Metabolic Daily, Akkermansia, and a GLP-1 probiotic - are formulated to fuel and maintain the gut lining, support immunity, relieve gas and bloating, and help keep blood glucose in a healthy range, differentiated by double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials rather than off-the-shelf probiotic blends. Pendulum is a direct-to-consumer health and supplement brand and is a portfolio company of DCVC; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.description: Talkspace is a New York City-based online behavioral healthcare company founded in 2012 by Oren Frank and Roni Frank that delivers virtual therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through video, voice, messaging, and live chat. The platform connects users with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers across all 50 U.S. states, covering more than 150 mental health conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder, OCD, PTSD, insomnia, postpartum depression, and substance use. Service lines include individual therapy for adults, teen therapy (ages 13-17), couples therapy, psychiatry with prescription management, and specialized programs for LGBTQIA+, military/veteran, and senior populations, plus the women's mental health program Chapters. Talkspace is in-network with major payers such as Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Optum, Blue Cross Blue Shield, TRICARE, and Medicare, and sells B2B solutions (Talkspace for Business) to employers, payers, benefit consultants, educational institutions, and government agencies. The company markets Precision Therapy, an internal machine-learning and NLP system used to match members to providers and surface clinical signal. Talkspace went public on NASDAQ under ticker TALK on June 23, 2021 via a SPAC merger with Hudson Executive Investment Corp, and was acquired by Universal Health Services on March 9, 2026. Talkspace does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository; integrations with payers, EAPs, and benefits platforms are delivered through private partnership channels, and the platform is HIPAA, HITECH, and GDPR compliant.

Augmedix's GitHub presence consists of internal QA, scribe-app base, and ambient API automation repositories; there is no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification — integration with Augmedix is handled through enterprise EHR partnerships and the Commure clinician platform rather than a self-service developer surface.

Its cellular-enabled vitals hubs and connected medical devices — blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, glucometers, thermometers, and scales — let patients transmit vital-sign readings to electronic health record (EHR) systems without WiFi, broadband, a smartphone, or app setup, targeting elderly, low-income, rural, and low-tech-literacy populations. Health systems and digital health organizations use Stel across the care continuum, from wellness and chronic-care management to hospital-at-home. Stel is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

companies.name: Care GP
companies.description: Care GP is a Sydney-based healthcare technology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building a suite of AI agents that automate the administrative and operational work of Australian general practice clinics. Its products include Samantha (medical document allocation that files inbound emails, faxes, and scans), Veronica (24/7 inbound and outbound phone and booking management), and a Billing beta for billing and debt-collection automation. Care GP states it is ISO 27001 certified with onshore Australian data storage, multi-factor authentication, and encryption, and reports serving 400+ clinic operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a customer web application (agent.caregp.com.au) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition.

companies.name: 7 Cups
companies.description: 7 Cups is an online emotional support and mental health platform founded in July 2013 by psychologist Glen Moriarty (Y Combinator S13) and based in Palo Alto, California. It connects people seeking help with trained volunteer "listeners" for free, anonymous, 24/7 one-to-one active-listening chat, and also offers community forums, group support chat rooms, self-help growth paths, and affordable online therapy with licensed therapists via messaging. The service reports reaching tens of millions of people across roughly 190 countries, supported by hundreds of thousands of trained volunteer listeners, and sells organizational solutions for schools, employers, and health plans. 7 Cups does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Alodokter

This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from the provider's own public web surface; Alodokter does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI at this time, so this profile focuses on company identity, legal and support surfaces, and domain security posture.

The company operates collaborative care-team clinics across Tennessee, Florida, and Texas, accepts most major insurance plans including Medicaid, and emphasizes longer appointments and whole-person (mental, physical, social) care. Diana Health is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes a consumer marketing and appointment-booking website but no public developer API; this profile is enriched with identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Easyhealth

Its Preventative Care Platform combines a hybrid visit model (in-home medical assistants paired with virtual nurse practitioners), Health Information Exchange integration, and real-time data dashboards for health plans to close HEDIS/care gaps, complete annual wellness visits, run preventive screenings, and manage chronic conditions such as cardiovascular, respiratory, diabetes, kidney, and behavioral health. EasyHealth emphasizes reaching underserved and hard-to-reach populations, claiming roughly 40% member engagement versus traditional sub-10% rates. The company is backed by Anthemis and QED Investors and is profiled here as an API Evangelist network company. EasyHealth publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

companies.name: Infervision
companies.description: Infervision is a medical artificial intelligence company that builds AI-powered medical imaging and clinical decision-support software for hospitals and healthcare providers. Its InferRead diagnostic suite assists radiologists with CT and DR reading across lung nodule detection, chest abnormality detection, coronary artery stenosis, stroke and hemorrhage triage, rib fracture identification, and pneumonia triage, while the InferOperate suite provides 3D reconstruction for thoracic, liver, and urological surgical planning. Additional platforms include InferCare for patient management and image follow-up, InferScholar for AI-enabled medical research, and the InferMatrix medical application platform. The company holds FDA 510(k) clearance for InferRead CT Lung, has filed 380+ patents and published 330+ peer-reviewed papers, and operates across 30+ countries. Infervision was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

companies.name: Inofab
companies.description: Inofab Health (a Clario company) is a digital respiratory health company headquartered in Ankara, Turkey, building connected spirometry and inhaler devices with cloud software for the home-based and clinical management of chronic respiratory conditions including asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis. Its product line spans the SpiroHome Personal portable ultrasonic spirometer, the SpiroClinic Pro and SpiroClinic Compact clinical-grade spirometers with EHR integration, the SpiroCloud web dashboard that collects and analyzes data from all connected SpiroHome and SpiroClinic devices, and the SpiroHaler smart inhaler attachments for medication adherence. Inofab was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: KiddoWear
companies.description: KiddoWear (now operating as Kiddo Health) is a pediatric healthcare technology company that offers a connected care platform for capturing and sharing health data for children with physical and behavioral health challenges. The platform combines biometric tracking of 12+ biomarkers (respiration, heart rate, stress scores, and sleep), family journaling of behavior and health status between visits, educational family resources, care navigation that integrates with medical records and clinical workflows, and a provider dashboard that surfaces insights and real-time health trends. Kiddo Health serves behavioral health conditions such as ADHD and autism spectrum disorder and metabolic conditions such as childhood obesity and diabetes, bridging gaps between families, providers, and care teams across health plans, health systems, and employers. A Techstars-backed portfolio company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Microhealth
companies.description: Microhealth is a Y Combinator (S15) digital-health company building digital therapeutics and connected patient-provider networks for people living with rare bleeding disorders such as hemophilia and for sickle cell disease. Its products let patients track, manage, and share their treatment journey while giving clinicians real-time monitoring between visits, and it aggregates anonymized real-world evidence for life-science and pharmaceutical research. Products include Microhealth Bleeding Disorders (patient) and Rare Bleeding Disorders HCP (clinician dashboard), Microhealth SCD and SCD HCP for sickle cell disease, and life-science research tooling. The company validates interventions through clinical studies toward regulatory clearance as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD). Its hemophilia network is reported to cover roughly a third of US patients and providers in the specialty, with pharmaceutical clients including Sanofi, Bayer, Novo Nordisk, Biogen, and Roche. Microhealth is a patient- and clinician-facing application platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

Its proprietary midsole is designed to dissipate and disperse impact energy outward rather than returning it into the joints, which the company markets for fatigue and pain reduction. The product lineup includes the AntiGrav1, AntiGrav2, and AG3 recovery shoes, the Gales Pro and Gales Frontline workforce and healthcare lines, and standalone recovery insoles. STAND+ is APMA (American Podiatric Medical Association) certified and HSA/FSA eligible through a Truemed partnership. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (standshoes.com) with no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Zwift
companies.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

companies.name: AppliedVR
companies.description: AppliedVR is a virtual reality therapeutics company that combines immersive technology with proven cognitive behavioral and behavioral-science techniques to treat medical conditions, with a focus on chronic pain. Its lead product, RelieVRx, is the first FDA-authorized prescription VR device for chronic lower back pain, delivering automated, self-administered cognitive behavioral therapy in the patient's home. AppliedVR also offers the SustainVR and ITx immersive therapeutics platform and the AVR Pathway patient-support system, and validates its products through clinical academic research. The company operates as a regulated digital-therapeutics / medical-device business rather than a developer-facing API platform, so it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Cera
companies.description: Cera is a United Kingdom-based digital-first home healthcare company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, that describes itself as Europe's largest provider of in-home care. Cera delivers home care, live-in care, nurse-led and complex care, extra-care housing, supported living, and specialist learning-disability and autism support, all wrapped around a proprietary digital platform that uses data analytics and machine learning so its network of carers can collect, monitor, and react to vital-sign and health-condition changes in real time. Cera positions this technology as a remote-monitoring and predictive layer that surfaces deterioration in health earlier and reduces hospitalisations across its United Kingdom home-care operations. As of this review Cera exposes no public developer portal, no self-serve REST API, and no HL7 FHIR endpoint or CapabilityStatement; its platform is an internal, operator-facing product delivered through consumer and carer mobile apps rather than a documented partner API. This profile is an honest identity-only stub recording the absence of a public API surface for a United Kingdom telehealth-adjacent home-care provider.

companies.name: Denta
companies.description: Denta is a San Francisco-based dental practice management and automation platform, founded by Jack Beecher (Jack Beecher LLC, dba Denta) and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). Positioned as "the dental practice that runs itself," Denta embeds AI into dental organizations to automate back-office operations: it ingests fragmented data from a practice's existing software, provides analytics so dentists can understand their business, and runs in the background to handle administrative work such as insurance payment posting. Its roadmap includes all-in-one native practice management software and an "autonomous dental practice." As of this profile Denta publishes a marketing site, a blog, and login and legal pages, but no public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface has been located.

companies.name: EyeLights
companies.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

companies.name: Karius
companies.description: Karius is an infectious disease diagnostics company that applies clinical metagenomics and machine learning to microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) circulating in the bloodstream, detecting pathogens that conventional culture-based testing misses. Its CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory runs the Karius Spectrum blood test, which screens a single blood draw for more than 1,000 bacteria, fungi, DNA viruses, and parasites, and the Karius Focus BAL test, which detects more than 500 pathogens in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid for lung infections.
