companies.description: Loop Health is an India-based health assurance and group insurance company, founded in 2018 by Mayank Kale and Amrit Singh and headquartered in Pune. It combines traditional group hospitalization insurance with unlimited primary care, telemedicine, wellness programs, mental-health counseling, and an Employee Assistance Program, delivered to employers and their teams through asset-light clinics and a member app. Backed by General Catalyst, Elevation Capital and Y Combinator, Loop serves 1,250+ companies and 950,000+ members across India. Mahmee works with major insurers such as Aetna, Cigna, Kaiser Permanente, and United Healthcare, and focuses on reducing maternal health disparities. Backed by General Catalyst, Memora is migrating onto the Commure platform at commure.com/engage.

Pearl reports serving 5,000+ providers across 40+ states, managing roughly 250,000 beneficiaries. Its lead product is Spydia (diazepam nasal spray), Japan's first domestically developed intranasal anti-seizure agent, approved in June 2025 and administrable outside medical facilities. Originally funded by SoftBank Vision Fund (Series C, March 2025), Aculys was acquired by and became part of the Viatris Group in October 2025. Aculys publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained for network completeness and identity.

companies.name: Lyra Health
companies.description: Lyra Health is a Burlingame, California enterprise mental health benefits company founded in 2015 that provides employer-sponsored behavioral health care to more than 20 million members across a network of 30,000+ providers in over 200 countries and territories. The platform combines preventive self-care resources, coaching, evidence-based therapy, medication management, family and pediatric services, and specialized acute care delivered through a benefits-administration model sold to large employers and health plans rather than directly to consumers. Lyra's product surface includes the Lyra App for members, the Lyra Empower AI-powered care platform launched in 2025, Centers of Excellence for pediatric mental health and neurodiversity, a manager coaching program, and a clinical-grade AI guide. Customers include Salesforce, Lululemon, Morgan Stanley, Genentech, Starbucks, JE Dunn, VCA, and the School District of Philadelphia, and in March 2026 the company became Workday Wellness's preferred mental health partner. Lyra acquired pediatric and family mental health provider Bend Health in July 2025. Lyra is led by CEO Jennifer Schulz, with Jenny Gonsalves as Chief Product & Technology Officer, Alethea Varra as Chief Clinical Officer, and co-founder Bob Kocher, MD on the board. The company's revenue model is per-member-per- month employer contracts plus utilization-based clinical billing; Lyra does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or self-service API, and its only public GitHub repository is an internal fork of an unrelated infrastructure module. All employer, member, HRIS/eligibility, SSO, and EHR integrations are negotiated and delivered through the Lyra customer success and implementation teams rather than through a self-serve developer surface.

companies.name: Octave
companies.description: Octave (Octave Online Therapy) is a modern behavioral and mental health company providing personalized, evidence-based therapy — individual, couples, and family therapy, plus Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and specialized Centers of Excellence for perinatal/postpartum mental health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Care is delivered virtually and in-person across 20+ U.S. states, with in-network insurance coverage, a therapy cost calculator, therapist matching, and a secure client portal. Octave is a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures. Octave publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web surface, a provider-published llms.txt, and its domain-security posture.

companies.name: Sectra
companies.description: Sectra is a Swedish medical technology company providing an enterprise imaging platform (PACS/VNA) for radiology, pathology, cardiology, orthopaedics, and other -ologies. Integration is delivered through established healthcare interoperability standards rather than a single open developer API - DICOM and DICOMweb for imaging, HL7 for orders/results messaging, IHE XDS for cross-enterprise document sharing, FHIR/FHIRcast for clinical context synchronization, and a Web Content API for embedding third-party content and applications into the diagnostic viewer. AI and third-party applications integrate through the Sectra Amplifier Marketplace / Amplifier Services ecosystem. Sectra's API and integration surface is partner- and customer-gated (deployed per-site, no public self-service developer portal); the API entries below are honestly modeled from Sectra's documented standards and interfaces, not scraped from an open OpenAPI catalog. Sectra also authored the first open-source FHIRcast sandbox and reference implementation.

companies.name: Daleela
companies.description: Daleela, by MotherBeing, is an AI-powered women's health application for the MENA region that combines medically-verified guidance with clinical services. The app offers a privacy-first AI health assistant whose answers are reviewed and approved by women's-health specialists, period and cycle tracking that monitors menstrual cycles and hormonal phases with personalized lifestyle recommendations, on-demand doctor consultations connecting users with specialists in gynecology, dermatology, nutrition, and sexual health within 24 hours, and expert-led educational programs covering hormones, fertility, and fitness. Daleela is distributed as a consumer mobile application on iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play). It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a consumer mobile product it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

companies.name: Doccla
companies.description: Doccla is a UK-founded virtual care platform delivering remote patient monitoring and virtual wards across Europe. It combines pre-configured, Bluetooth-connected medical devices, a patient app, and a clinician dashboard to monitor patients at home, reducing hospital admissions and freeing bed capacity for health systems. The platform integrates bidirectionally with electronic health record (EHR) systems, including Oracle Cerner for the Northwest London Virtual Hospital, and is deployed with NHS trusts and European providers. Doccla holds ISO 27001 and ISO 13485 certifications, UKCA and CE medical-device marks, is GDPR compliant, and is registered with the UK Care Quality Commission (CQC). No public developer API or portal is published at this time; integration is delivered via managed EHR and medical-device connections.

companies.name: Felmo
companies.description: felmo (felmo GmbH) is a mobile veterinary practice (mobile Tierarztpraxis) headquartered in Berlin, Germany that brings licensed veterinarians directly to pet owners' homes for dogs and cats. Founded in 2019 by CEO Philip Trockels, felmo operates across Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf and 25+ additional German cities, and has treated 300,000+ animals with 8,000+ home visits per month via 140+ mobile vets. Services include preventive care and consultations, examinations and diagnostics, laboratory and imaging, surgical procedures (including a fully-equipped mobile operating vehicle / OP-Wagen), dental medicine and holistic pet care, billed per the German veterinary fee schedule (GOT). Customers book appointments, access medical records and lab results, receive reminders, and message support through the felmo iOS and Android app. felmo is backed by HV Capital and additional venture investors. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity and web properties.

companies.name: Oncimmune
companies.description: Oncimmune is a biotechnology company specializing in antibody and autoantibody biomarker discovery for precision medicine. Its proprietary ImmunoINSIGHTS platform screens against 9,000+ human antigens using Luminex xMAP bead-based multiplexed immunoassay technology, minimal sample volumes, high-throughput automated robotic workflows, and proprietary machine-learning algorithms to identify immune-system signatures across immuno-oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease. Products include the ImmunoINSIGHTS 2K targeted panels, custom biomarker discovery services, and bioinformatics/data-science multiomics integration. Oncimmune was acquired by Alden Scientific in July 2025. The company operates as a research and discovery services provider and does not publish a public developer or API platform.

companies.name: X Zell
companies.description: X-ZELL is a Thailand-based medical technology company (Y Combinator W15) building a multiplex cytopathology product ecosystem that combines cryofixation, immunostaining, and digital imaging to turn limited cytology specimens into data-rich diagnostic workflows. Its Cryosuite platform pairs a Cryofixator and Cryostainer for specimen processing and automated staining, alongside Cryophore multiplex antibody panels for pleural fluid, ascitic fluid, and tumor-origin analysis, validated conjugated antibodies, and ISO 13485-certified reagent and OEM manufacturing. Founded by physician-scientist Sebastian Punyaratabandhu Bhakdi, the company originated in rare-cell detection (Circulating Endothelial Cells). It is a hardware, reagent, and laboratory-instrument business and publishes no public API, developer platform, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

companies.name: Eve
companies.description: Eve (eve.legal) is a legal AI platform built by Butler Labs, Inc. for plaintiff law firms. Marketed as "the only legal AI that works your whole case with you," Eve 2.0 is positioned as a proactive AI workforce that spans the full plaintiff case lifecycle — intake and evaluation, pre-litigation drafting (medical chronologies, demand letters), litigation discovery (propounding and responding), and case auditing. The platform is organized around three product surfaces: Eve Agents (intake & evaluation, AI voice agent, medical overviews, demand letters, drafting, propounding discovery, responding to discovery), Eve Auditor (nightly audit of the active caseload for missed value drivers such as TBIs, MRIs ordered but not taken, and mass-tort eligibility), and Eve Analyst (announced as "coming soon"). Eve targets personal injury and labor & employment plaintiff firms and claims to be used by 1000+ firms with reported outcomes including a 250% year-over-year revenue increase, 2.5x case capacity, 90% faster demand letter generation, and a 4.9/5 G2 rating. Eve is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, with case data encrypted, isolated per-firm, and never used to train shared models. The company is led by founder & CEO Jay Madheswaran (formerly Rubrik, Lightspeed Venture Partners), co-founder & CPO Matt Noe, and co-founder & Head of Engineering David Zeng, and has raised $164M+ from venture investors. Eve is a closed B2B SaaS application; as of this profile there is no public developer API, no public OpenAPI/AsyncAPI documentation, no `docs.eve.legal` developer portal, no SDKs, and no public repositories under the `eve-legal` GitHub organization (the org exists with zero public repos as of May 2026). All access is through the Eve web application following a sales-led "Schedule a call" / "Book a Demo" motion.

companies.name: Olive AI
companies.description: Olive AI was a Columbus, Ohio healthcare automation company founded in 2012 by Sean Lane (originally as CrossChx, rebranded to Olive in 2017). The company built robotic process automation (RPA), AI, and workflow tooling aimed at the healthcare revenue cycle — including a "digital workforce" marketed as "Olive" that automated repetitive administrative tasks in hospitals and health systems. Olive's portfolio centered on clearinghouse and patient access automation, prior authorization automation, claims status checks, eligibility verification, and process mining for revenue-cycle optimization. At its peak Olive raised more than $900M and reached a $4B valuation, but a series of strategic missteps, layoffs, and cash burn forced an orderly wind-down. In late 2023 Olive sold its clearinghouse and patient access business to Waystar, and in early 2024 sold its prior authorization business to Humata Health, then ceased operations. The Olive AI brand is no longer active and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; surviving capabilities live on inside Waystar and Humata Health.

companies.name: VaultDragon
companies.description: VaultDragon (Vault Dragon Pte Ltd) is a Singapore-based digital healthcare company building end-to-end practice-management software for clinics and medical providers across Southeast Asia and China. Its product suite includes DragonHub, an end-to-end clinic-management platform covering appointment scheduling, patient tracking, electronic health records, inventory and invoicing; DragonCare, a patient-facing web app for self-booking, reminders and access to medical history; DragonInsights, an on-demand business- intelligence and analytics layer; and DragonLab, a laboratory information system automating the workflow from sample receipt to report delivery. VaultDragon serves 650+ healthcare providers across Singapore, China, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia. The platform is delivered as a hosted SaaS (hub.vaultdragon.com) backed by a private, authenticated internal API; the company currently publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or client SDKs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

companies.name: Bayesian Health
companies.description: Bayesian Health is a real-time clinical intelligence company whose adaptive AI platform monitors hospitalized patients continuously inside the electronic health record, surfacing only the patients who need attention and giving clinicians evidence-based guidance to act. Its flagship Targeted Real-Time Early Warning System (TREWS) reads full patient charts — labs, vitals, and clinical notes — to detect sepsis and other deterioration hours earlier while cutting alert volume, and in May 2026 became the first-ever FDA-cleared continuous AI sepsis monitor. Founded by Johns Hopkins professor Suchi Saria, the company deploys through direct EHR partnerships with Epic and Cerner rather than a public developer API, and is backed by a16z.

companies.name: MDClone
companies.description: MDClone is a healthcare data company whose ADAMS platform gives health systems, life-sciences organizations, and researchers self-service access to explore, analyze, and share clinical data. Its signature capability is a synthetic-data engine that generates non-reversible, artificially created datasets which preserve the statistical characteristics and correlations of real patient data without carrying any protected health information (PHI), removing re-identification risk. The platform lets users organize source data, generate synthetic versions on demand, run analytics, and apply generative AI to accelerate research and improve patient outcomes. MDClone is enterprise/customer-gated: access, support, and any programmatic data-export API are provisioned to licensed customers rather than published as a public developer program.

companies.name: Regard
companies.description: Regard is an AI-powered clinical diagnosis and documentation platform for hospitals and health systems. It reviews 100% of a patient's electronic health record (EHR) to surface and recommend evidence-supported diagnoses, then generates clinical documentation at the point of care. Regard positions itself around "earning revenue through better care, not queries," spanning clinical notes, mid-revenue-cycle denial prevention and revenue capture, HCC risk-adjustment capture, and screening for care gaps. The company reports 12.9M+ recommended diagnoses accepted by clinicians and $50M+ in revenue generated for health systems. Regard integrates directly with EHRs rather than exposing a public developer API; its Health IT Module is ONC 2015 Cures Update certified. Backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Maven Clinic
companies.description: Maven Clinic is a virtual clinic for women's and family health serving 2,300+ employers and 28 million covered lives globally. Programs span fertility and family building, maternity and newborn care, parenting and pediatrics, menopause and midlife health, GLP-1 and hormone care, and a 30+ specialty virtual clinic. Maven sells primarily B2B through employer benefits and health plan partnerships, with go-to-market surfaces for employers, health plans, and benefits consultants. Maven's care model is validated by 40+ peer-reviewed studies and Milliman-audited outcomes. No public developer API has been identified - partner integrations are handled via gated employer and health plan onboarding. This entry catalogs the company surface for the API Evangelist index.

Philips transitioned from a diversified electronics conglomerate to a dedicated healthcare technology leader and operates the HealthSuite Digital Platform (HSDP) as its cloud-based platform for connected health applications. HSDP exposes Identity & Access Management, Provisioning, IoT/Connect, Foundation, Cognitive, Clinical Data, and Notification building blocks to enable consumer health and professional healthcare applications, but access is gated behind a customer portal at www.hsdp.io with developer documentation distributed to authenticated customers and partners rather than the open public web. Philips also operates vertical Connected Care offerings (Patient Monitoring, eICU/Capsule, Sleep & Respiratory Care/SimplyGo, IntelliSpace) layered on HSDP. The legacy Philips Hue lighting API is no longer a Philips offering - Hue has been spun off into Signify and is published at developers.meethue.com.

companies.name: Blue Fever
companies.description: Blue Fever is a social and mental-health app for young people that pairs a judgment-free peer community with "Blue," an AI emotional-support companion, under the tagline "A place to feel seen, not be seen." Users share thoughts, moods, and creative expression and receive support from both community members and the AI companion, alongside curated wellness resources and crisis support. The app is available on iOS and Android, has been featured as an Apple App of the Day, and carries a 4.6 App Store rating. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer application with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: Fuchsia
companies.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.description: Siren is a digital health company that makes temperature-monitoring smart socks to prevent diabetic foot ulcers. The seamless, machine-washable socks require no charging or smartphone; embedded sensors continuously track foot temperature to detect the early inflammation that precedes an ulcer, and licensed nurses review the data and alert the patient's healthcare provider. Siren pairs the hardware with a remote patient monitoring service billed through providers and payers, and operates as a HIPAA-regulated healthcare business rather than a developer platform. It is backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures. As surveyed for the API Evangelist network, Siren publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

The company is a portfolio company of Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. companies.description: Vivid Vision is a digital vision care company that builds VR- and software-based tools for diagnosing and treating binocular vision disorders. Its products include a vision training system for amblyopia (lazy eye), strabismus, and convergence insufficiency; Vivid Vision Perimetry (VVP), a VR-based visual field test used as an endpoint in ophthalmology clinical trials for geographic atrophy, AMD, and glaucoma; and EYEBAB VT therapeutic exercises for clinical settings. Founded in 2014, the platform has been used by more than 100,000 patients across 50+ countries through eye-care practices and clinics. Vivid Vision is backed by Uncork Capital. The company is a patient- and clinician-facing vision-care provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

(NYSE: HIMS) is a direct-to-consumer telehealth platform headquartered in San Francisco that connects consumers with licensed providers and ships personalized treatments across men's and women's health categories. Hims serves men with offerings spanning sexual health, hair loss, mental health, dermatology, and weight loss; Hers serves women with birth control, hair, skin, mental health, and weight management; both brands include compounded GLP-1 weight-loss programs. International expansion has been driven by the acquisitions of ZAVA (Europe, 2025) and Eucalyptus Health (Australia, 2026). Hims & Hers is primarily a consumer D2C product; no public developer API has been identified, and B2B and partner integrations are gated. companies.description: AKASA is a generative AI company for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), building AI-powered products that automate coding, clinical documentation integrity (CDI), prior authorization status, and claim status work for hospitals and health systems. Its platform includes the Prebill Optimization Suite (Coding Optimizer and CDI Optimizer), AI Advisor, Auth Status, and Claim Status, trained on millions of clinical and financial documents. AKASA reports serving 650+ hospitals and 6,500+ outpatient facilities across all 50 states, with customers citing reductions in A/R days and hundreds of monthly staff hours saved. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

companies.name: Alamar Biosciences
companies.description: Alamar Biosciences is a precision proteomics company advancing early disease detection through its NULISA platform and ARGO HT System. NULISA (NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay) combines a sequential immunocomplex capture-and-release mechanism with next-generation sequencing readout to deliver attomolar sensitivity and high-plex multiplexing for protein biomarker discovery, validation, and translational research. The fully automated ARGO HT System processes up to 288 samples per batch with under 30 minutes of hands-on time, supporting large-cohort studies across neurology, immunology, and oncology. Alamar was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a life-sciences instrument and assay provider rather than a public-API company, so this profile captures identity, published web surface, and domain-security posture. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface was found.

companies.name: Illuminate Education
companies.description: Illuminate Education is a K-12 education technology company providing assessment, data analytics, and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) tools to schools and districts. companies.description: Open mHealth is a nonprofit, community-driven initiative that develops open standards and open-source software for making patient-generated health data interoperable across mobile apps, wearables, clinical systems, and electronic health records. Its core contribution is a library of clinically validated JSON Schema data point schemas — covering physical activity, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, body weight, blood glucose, and other vital signs — with the sleep, physical-activity, and metadata schemas now superseded by IEEE 1752.1, the IEEE standard for Mobile Health Data co-shepherded by the Open mHealth community. Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

companies.name: Atropos Health

Its flagship platform GENEVA OS (Generative Evidence Acceleration Operating System) is a federated, cloud-agnostic operating system that installs behind the customer's firewall, ingests longitudinal patient records as in-memory patient-timeline objects, and exposes a Temporal Query Language (TQL) and Advanced Cohort Engine (ACE) for rapid observational analyses without moving PHI. On top of GENEVA OS, Atropos offers ChatRWD, a conversational chat-to-database application that generates full observational studies from natural-language clinical questions, the Atropos Evidence Agent (an agentic AI deployed at Stanford Health Care and developed in collaboration with Microsoft to surface RWE directly inside clinical workflows and notes), Green Button (the original on-demand consult-style evidence service that gave rise to the company), Forge (study automation), and Alexandria, marketed as the world's largest body of precision evidence-based findings with 33M+ entries used for clinical decision support and LLM training. The company sells into health systems (pharmacy, research informatics, value-based care, GME) and life sciences (brand planning, HEOR, medical affairs, R&D, commercial analytics, precision-medicine AI/ML), is backed by Valtruis, Emerson Collective, Breyer Capital, McKinsey Ventures, Cencora Ventures, Presidio Ventures, Merck Global Health Innovation, Samsung Next, and others, and partners with Stanford Health Care, Mayo Clinic Platform, and Microsoft. Atropos has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; GENEVA OS, TQL, ACE, ChatRWD, and the Evidence Agent are proprietary enterprise software delivered under contract to health-system and life-sciences customers, and the company's public GitHub org contains only forks (FAISS, HELM, security-policy-templates, terraform-aws-github-runner) and a small number of internal research notebooks rather than any shippable client library.

companies.name: Mendel AI

Hypercube is offered as three productized experiences — Hypercube Cohort for patient cohort discovery (with funnel-style criteria analysis and direct integration to clinicaltrials.gov), Hypercube Analyst for AI-driven analysis of structured and unstructured real-world data, and Build Your Own Hypercube for custom clinical-data queries. The platform integrates with enterprise data warehouses (Databricks, Snowflake) and BI tools (Tableau, Qlik), and is available through the AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Azure Marketplace, and natively on the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. Mendel serves pharma, providers, payers, and research organizations including Quest Diagnostics, Boston Scientific, Gatehouse Bio, and the University of Pennsylvania, with published evidence in oncology trial prescreening. Mendel has no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source GitHub repositories; integration is delivered through enterprise contracts and cloud-marketplace deployments.

companies.name: Surtr Defense Systems
companies.description: Surtr Defense Systems is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company building ParallaxOS, an open operating system for counter-UAS (counter-drone) command-and-control. Surtr positions itself outside the incumbent C2 tension by not competing with hardware partners on contracts and not monetizing partner data: hardware partners decide what data the platform sees, customers decide what data is kept, and every byte is visible to partners and customers in real time. ParallaxOS ingests any sensor (radar, RF, EO/IR, acoustic) over open defense-interoperability standards such as NATO SAPIENT, Link 16, Cursor on Target, and ATAK; tasks any compatible kinetic, EW, or directed-energy effector with human-in-the-loop authorization on every engagement; and performs multi-sensor fusion, autonomous track correlation, and AI threat classification at millisecond latency on the tactical edge. Customer data, integration code, and decisions remain the customer's, deployed on-prem or in GovCloud. Founded by Anshul Ahluwalia (CEO, ex-Shield AI) and Cameron Fiore (CTO, ex-Anduril, ex-Shield AI). Its recorded domain kiira.io is no longer controlled by the company — it now redirects to an unrelated third-party site — so this profile reflects the company's last-known (archived, Dec 2024) state and is treated as a defunct / lapsed lead.

companies.name: Lumius
companies.description: Lumius is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) medical-imaging startup building fast, smart, accessible real-time 3D ultrasound systems — described as "a 3D camera for the body." The technology aims to move ultrasound beyond traditional 2D imaging to intelligent, AI-assisted 3D visualization across larger volumes, with an initial focus on vascular access and central-line placement (where roughly half of first attempts fail among new clinicians) and future targets including blood-clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. The company partners with academic institutions such as Duke University and Columbia University. Lumius is a hardware/device company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform; its products are pre-market and not intended for medical use. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio lead and has been reviewed by the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Medir
companies.description: Medir is a South Korean digital-health company behind Medb (메듭), a non-face-to-face (telemedicine) and prescription-drug delivery platform that connects patients, doctors, hospitals and pharmacies. Through the Medb mobile app, patients receive 100% video consultations with physicians and have their prescribed medications delivered to their door — often within roughly 30 minutes to two hours — with no separate service fee beyond the standard consultation charge. Medir is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. The business operates as a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network pending any future API surface.

companies.name: MycroFriends
companies.description: MycroFriends is a consumer health and wellness company that helps people become healthier through education and coaching centered on the connection between the human microbiome, nutrition, and overall health. Founded by George Cigale (previously founder of the online tutoring company Tutor.com) and headquartered in New York City, the company launched via a 2017 crowdfunding campaign and works with scientists, physicians, dietitians, and technologists to deliver microbiome education, personalized nutritional and lifestyle guidance, and access to expert health coaches. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass MycroFriends publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface, and its former website resolves only to a default (unconfigured) Azure App Service host.

companies.name: Onkos Surgical
companies.description: Onkos Surgical is a privately held surgical oncology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey, focused on innovative solutions for musculoskeletal oncology and complex orthopaedic procedures. Built on a digital platform grounded in patient imaging analysis, personalized surgical planning and advanced 3D printing, Onkos develops limb salvage systems, My3D personalized solutions, uDesign on-demand personalized surgical plans, and antibacterial-coated implants for tumor and revision orthopaedic applications. The company received the first FDA De Novo approval of an antibacterial coating for tumor and revision orthopaedic implants. Onkos does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surfaces are the corporate website, a product Instructions-for-Use (IFU) documentation library, and a surgeon training portal.

companies.name: Patient IO
companies.description: Patient IO (legal entity Filament Labs, Inc.) was an Austin, Texas care coordination and patient engagement platform founded in 2013 by Jason Bornhorst, Colin Anawaty, and Brian Gambs out of the Techstars Austin accelerator. Its API-first mobile platform connected health systems with patients between visits to support the transition to value-based care. athenahealth acquired Patient IO in August 2016 and its architecture became the foundation of athenahealth's patient-facing athenawell application. The standalone product, developer program, and public API surface have since been retired; patientio.com now serves only a placeholder page and its mail is handled by athenahealth.

companies.name: Pine Medical
companies.description: Pine Medical was a telehealth provider that offered a medication-supported weight-loss program pairing licensed clinicians with prescription therapies and ongoing patient coaching. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. An enrichment probe on 2026-07-20 found the public website (pinemedical.com) announcing that Pine Medical wound down its medication-supported weight-loss program effective March 30, 2024, and redirects former patients to alternative providers and insurance-covered options. No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found.

companies.name: Roclub
companies.description: roclub (roclub GmbH) is a German health-tech company operating a remote-control platform for diagnostic medical imaging. Its software lets healthcare organizations perform MRI and CT examinations remotely ("Remote Scanning") and support on-site technicians from anywhere ("Remote Support"), with real-time screen sharing and device control across multi-vendor scanners (Siemens, Philips, GE, Canon). roclub also runs a marketplace of qualified medical technologists ("rocStars") who can be booked on demand, together with session documentation, scheduling, and built-in liability insurance ("roCover"). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation was found during enrichment.

Its portfolio spans tumor markers, HPV detection, autoimmune antibodies, infectious disease, thrombosis and reproductive-health assays across flow-fluorescence, chemiluminescence, real-time PCR / molecular, and clinical-chemistry platforms (TESMI analyzer family). The company was listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board in April 2017 (ticker 300642) and counts Qiming Venture Partners among its early investors. Tellgen is a medical-device and laboratory-reagent manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Yoderm
companies.description: YoDerm was a consumer telehealth company operating an online dermatology platform that let patients upload photos and a medical questionnaire, receive a personalized treatment plan from a U.S. board-certified dermatologist within 48 hours, and have prescriptions filled by mail-order pharmacy. Founded in Oakland, California around 2012, it rebranded to Apostrophe in 2019, was acquired by Hims & Hers Health (reported ~$190M), and ceased standalone operations in March 2025 when the parent folded dermatology into its main platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. YoDerm is a direct-to-consumer telehealth product with no public developer program, no documented API, and no OpenAPI, MCP, webhook, or SDK surface; the yoderm.com domain now returns HTTP 503.

companies.name: Zhuhai DL Biotech (medicaldl)
companies.description: Zhuhai DL Biotech Co., Ltd. (Zhuhai Deer Bioengineering Co., Ltd., brand "DL" / 迪尔), founded in 2003 and based in Zhuhai, China, is a high-tech in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) enterprise specializing in the R&D, manufacturing, and service of microbial diagnostic instruments and reagents. Its product lines cover automated blood culture systems, automated bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (ID/AST), MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry microbial identification, automated staining, fluorescence immunoassay, and molecular diagnostics, serving over 5,000 clinical healthcare institutions across more than 50 countries. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or software integration surface — this is a diagnostic-hardware and reagent business, not a software/API provider.

The combined entity operates as Zimmer Biomet Holdings and no public APIs are published under the LVB Acquisition brand.

companies.name: Balderton Capital
companies.description: Balderton Capital is a London-headquartered venture capital firm focused exclusively on backing European-founded technology companies. Founded in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe and fully independent since 2007, Balderton is one of Europe's largest and most established venture firms, with over $7 billion in assets under management across dedicated early-stage and growth funds. The firm invests from Seed through Series B and follows on into growth stages, writing checks across sectors including fintech, artificial intelligence, B2B SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, digital health, gaming, marketplaces and climate. Balderton is known for a founder-centric model, running a dedicated founder wellbeing and performance platform and an executive/talent network to support portfolio companies. Notable investments over the firm's history include Revolut, GoCardless, Depop, Darktrace, Contentful, Dream Games, Wayve, Aircall, Citymapper, Talend, MySQL, Recorded Future, Sophia Genetics and The Hut Group (THG).

companies.name: Cybersecurity Standards
companies.description: Cybersecurity Standards captures the public, machine-readable, and reference frameworks that establish best practices for protecting information systems, networks, software, and data from cyber threats. The landscape is anchored by U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) publications such as the Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, SP 800-53 controls, SP 800-171 controls for controlled unclassified information, the Risk Management Framework (RMF), and the Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF SP 800-218); the international ISO/IEC 27001 / 27002 information security management standard family; the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Critical Security Controls and Benchmarks; the OWASP Top 10 and ASVS for application security; PCI DSS for payment data; HITRUST CSF for healthcare; SOC 2 trust services criteria; and FedRAMP / StateRAMP for cloud authorization. This index aggregates authoritative URLs, machine-readable artifacts (e.g., OSCAL), and cross-references for organizations building or auditing cybersecurity programs.

companies.name: DietlyAPI
companies.description: Food & nutrition data REST API with 4.2M+ foods, calories, macros, 17 micronutrients, barcode lookup, and confidence-ranked full-text search. Data primarily from Open Food Facts (ODbL), EU-hosted, with key-optional read access.

companies.name: EQT Ventures
companies.description: EQT Ventures is the early-stage venture capital business within EQT Group, launched in 2016 and operating out of Stockholm with investment-advisory offices in London, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, and the United States (San Francisco / New York); the funds themselves are domiciled in Luxembourg. The firm is a sector-agnostic, conviction-led lead investor that backs what it calls "Generation-Defining Companies" from pre-seed and seed through Series A and B, writing checks that reported ranges place between roughly EUR 1M and EUR 75M (most commonly EUR 2M-50M) and following on as companies scale. EQT Ventures has raised approximately EUR 2.3B across three funds (EQT Ventures I, II, and III) and is staffed largely by ex-founders and operators who provide hands-on support in addition to capital. Its focus spans AI, SaaS and developer tools, fintech, healthtech, climate and deeptech, robotics and aerospace, gaming, and consumer/marketplaces. Notable investments include Wolt, Depop, Typeform, AnyDesk, Netlify, Fly.io, Einride, Small Giant Games, Kry, and Beamery.

companies.name: Insight Partners
companies.description: Insight Partners is a global software-focused venture capital and private equity firm founded in 1995 by Jeff Horing and Jerry Murdock and headquartered in New York City, with additional offices in London, Tel Aviv, and Palo Alto. The firm invests in high-growth technology and software ScaleUp companies at every stage from early (Series A) through growth and late-stage pre-IPO, deploying checks that range from roughly $5M up to $500M+ and pairing capital with a dedicated in-house operations team (Insight Onsite) that provides talent, sales, marketing, and product expertise to accelerate scaling. Sector emphasis spans enterprise software broadly, including cybersecurity, fintech, AI/ML, DevOps, data infrastructure, and healthtech. With approximately $90B in regulatory assets under management as of 2025 and more than 875 companies backed worldwide, Insight is one of the largest technology investors in the world, with a portfolio and exit history that includes Twitter, Shopify, DocuSign, Wix, SentinelOne, HelloFresh, N26, Alteryx, and AppDynamics.

companies.name: Khosla Ventures
companies.description: Khosla Ventures is a Menlo Park, California venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Sun Microsystems co-founder Vinod Khosla. The firm backs bold, early, and impactful ventures, favoring contrarian deep-tech bets with world-class teams and a conviction-driven approach that deliberately accepts a high failure rate to capture transformative outcomes. Khosla invests across seed, early (Series A/B), and growth stages through its Seed Fund, Main Fund, and Opportunity (growth) Fund, writing checks that range from small seed positions to large growth rounds. Focus sectors span artificial intelligence, enterprise and consumer software, financial services and fintech, robotics and frontier/deep tech, aerospace and defense, climate and sustainability (clean energy, fusion, materials, agriculture), and digital health, medtech, diagnostics, and therapeutics. The firm manages roughly $16 billion in assets as of 2025 and is known for early investments in OpenAI, Stripe, Square/Block, DoorDash, Instacart, Affirm, Impossible Foods, GitLab, Okta, Rocket Lab, and QuantumScape. Headquarters are at 2128 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park, CA, with a primarily United States geographic focus and select global investments.

companies.name: Matrix Partners
companies.description: Matrix Partners (now branded simply "Matrix") is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1977 by Paul Ferri, investing from idea through Series A. Headquartered in San Francisco at 535 Mission Street with a long-standing East Coast office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the firm is run by former founders and company builders who describe themselves as "contrarians who invest with conviction," backing founders with deep technical expertise and a specific vision of the future. Matrix is a generalist early-stage investor across AI / frontier tech, B2B and enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthtech, infrastructure, and semiconductors, typically writing seed and Series A checks and leading rounds. Over nearly five decades the firm has backed foundational technology and consumer companies including Apple, HubSpot, Zendesk, Canva, Afterpay, Oculus, Fivetran, Flock Safety, Quora, Postmates, GOAT, and Suno, with a track record spanning semiconductors and networking through today's AI-native startups.

companies.name: New Enterprise Associates
companies.description: New Enterprise Associates (NEA) is one of the world's largest and longest-running venture capital firms, founded in 1977 by Dick Kramlich, Chuck Newhall, and Frank Bonsal. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in Timonium (Maryland), New York, and London, NEA invests across the full company lifecycle — "from idea to IPO" — spanning seed, Series A, and later growth rounds. The firm has raised over $27 billion in committed capital (as of December 31, 2024) and organizes into specialized practice groups across two core sectors: technology (enterprise software, consumer, fintech, AI, infrastructure) and healthcare (biopharma, life sciences, digital health, and medical devices). NEA is known for an active, hands-on partnership model and long-term support of category-defining companies, with a portfolio that has produced many notable IPOs and acquisitions including Cloudflare, MongoDB, Robinhood, Coursera, Databricks, Plaid, and Tempus.

companies.name: NextGen Healthcare
companies.description: NextGen Healthcare is a leading ambulatory care EHR and practice management platform providing REST and FHIR APIs for clinical data, scheduling, patient engagement, and healthcare interoperability. The platform offers Enterprise APIs comprising 400+ JSON-based RESTful routes covering EHR, practice management, and clinical workflows, as well as FHIR R4 Patient Access APIs, SMART on FHIR App Launch APIs, and Bulk FHIR APIs compliant with 21st Century Cures Act requirements. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 with authorization code and client credentials flows. Products support USCDI v1 data exchange, HL7 FHIR DSTU2 and R4 standards, and Mirth Connect integration engine for HL7-based interoperability.

companies.name: Regulatory Templates
companies.description: Pre-built templates, frameworks, and policy libraries for meeting regulatory compliance requirements across industries and jurisdictions including GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and more. Compliance platforms and API governance tools provide template-driven approaches to accelerate audit readiness, evidence collection, and risk management workflows.

companies.name: Sierra Ventures
companies.description: Sierra Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded by Peter Wendell in 1982 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley. The firm invests from inception through Series A in first-principles founders under the tagline "Conviction Before Consensus," writing checks of up to $5M at seed and up to $10M at Series A. Sierra's current investment thesis centers on the next wave of enterprise technology: Vertical AI (purpose-built AI for specific industries), Infrastructure AI, Frontier and Deep Tech, and Physical AI and Robotics, alongside a longstanding history in enterprise applications, digital health, SaaS, and security. Over its 40-plus-year history the firm has invested more than $2 billion across 13 early-stage funds, with its 13th fund closing in 2023 at $265 million, following Fund 12 at $215 million and Fund 11 at $170 million. Sierra reports 35 IPOs and hundreds of successful exits, having backed companies such as Elastic, Astronomer, Chronosphere, CourseHero, Q-CTRL, Spectro Cloud, Endor Labs, and Reflection AI. The firm is notable for its CXO Advisory Board of Fortune 1000 enterprise leaders who help portfolio companies land early customers. This profile tracks Sierra Ventures' identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: SoftBank Vision Fund
companies.description: SoftBank Vision Fund (managed by SoftBank Investment Advisers) is one of the world's largest technology-focused investment funds, launched in May 2017 by SoftBank Group and anchored by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. Now operating across two funds (SVF1 and SVF2) with combined assets under management reported at roughly $150B+, the fund pursues Masayoshi Son's long "AI economy" thesis, backing high-growth companies across the AI stack: hardware and semiconductors, the software infrastructure to gather, process and deploy data, and the applications built on top of it. It typically writes large late-stage growth checks (Series C/D and beyond, often $100M to several billion) into 300+ companies worldwide, spanning enterprise software, consumer internet, health tech, fintech, logistics, transportation, frontier tech, edtech and proptech across the Americas, EMEA and Asia. Headquartered in London, with major offices in the US and Asia, its portfolio includes many unicorns and household names such as Arm, ByteDance, and Aurora.

companies.name: Starting Line VC
companies.description: Starting Line is a Chicago-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2018 by Ezra Galston that invests first checks into consumer technology startups nationwide. The firm concentrates on consumer AI, consumer health and longevity, Gen Alpha / Gen Z, consumer mobile, consumer fintech, and consumer marketplaces — as well as the infrastructure that supports them. Starting Line typically writes first checks of $500K-$1.5M (optimally $750K-$1.25M into a ~$2.5M seed round), maintains a roughly 2:1 initial-to-reserves ratio, and makes about 6-8 new investments per year. It has raised three funds — Fund I ($17M, 2018), Fund II ($30M, 2021), and Fund III ($30M, 2023) — and is headquartered in Chicago with portfolio concentrations in Los Angeles, Austin, and New York. The firm is known for radical transparency, open-sourcing its operating manual, quarterly LP letters, and mental health policy on GitHub. Notable investments include Cameo, M1 Finance, Substack, Hungryroot, Shef, Soona, SpotHero (acquired by Uber), and Pretty Litter (acquired by Mars for ~$1B).

companies.name: Threshold Ventures
companies.description: Threshold Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California that backs founder-led technology companies at the threshold of breakout growth. Threshold is the 2019 rebrand of Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ), the storied Sand Hill Road firm founded in 1985; managing partners Emily Melton and Josh Stein spun the venture practice into an independent, focused fund. Threshold pursues a high-conviction strategy, concentrating on a small number of Series A and Series B investments and partnering hands-on with founders for the long term, frequently holding board seats through IPO and beyond. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health and healthcare, and AI. Its portfolio has produced 10 unicorns, 3 IPOs, and 17 acquisitions, and includes Box, Twilio, Redfin, Remitly, Doximity, Rippling, LaunchDarkly, Livongo, and Talkdesk. Threshold has invested in roughly 87 companies and raised a ~$250M fund following the rebrand.

companies.name: Web Standards
companies.description: Specifications and guidelines that define how web technologies should work, ensuring interoperability and consistency across browsers and platforms. Web standards are developed by organizations like W3C, WHATWG, IETF, and ECMA International. This topic covers the full landscape of web standards including HTML, CSS, JavaScript APIs, networking, security, graphics, media, and emerging technologies.
